Sports.title: Why Coventry, Tottenham and Aston Villa should not panic about their slow starts
Sports.content:
That optimism we feel at the start of a new season can be intoxicating. Whatever happened last season, there has been a whole summer to correct things. New signings, possibly a new manager, and new possibilities. What could go wrong? Oh, everything. Terrific. We’re only in mid-September, but that early optimism has melted away and been replaced by anxiety for some fans.

Coventry had every reason to look forward to the season, their first in the Premier League since 2001. They were coming off the back of a title-winning campaign in the Championship and were riding the crest of a wave. Now, though, they have fallen off their surfboard and are frantically trying to keep their heads above water as the ferocity of the top flight becomes increasingly apparent.

They are the only Premier League team without a point after four games and they are yet to even score a goal. In fairness, two of their games have been away to the two strongest sides in the league, Arsenal and Manchester City. Coventry were pretty impressive in the latter of those matches, too, and probably deserved something from it.

However, a 1-0 defeat at home to fellow promoted side Hull and a 5-0 thrashing at the hands of Brighton on Sunday have brought stark realisation that the Premier League is a tricky business. Taiwo Awoniyi’s red card in the second half against Brighton did not help, but they were already 2-0 down by then. When Lewis Dunk is bending efforts into the top corner from 30 yards, you know it isn’t going to be your day.

Coventry are the eighth promoted team to lose their first four games of a Premier League season. Only one avoided relegation: Southampton in 2012-13.

Looking at all the teams that have lost their first four game in a Premier League campaign, it is a little more comforting. Eighteen did that before Coventry and eight of them stayed up, the most recent of which was Everton in 2024-25.

We are not here to rub it in, though. We are here to try to provide hope. Somewhere in our sea of Premier League records, surely, we can find something to cheer up struggling teams?

For Coventry, look no further than Crystal Palace from the 2017-18 season. Under the management of Frank de Boer, they did not score or win a single point in their first five games. The Dutchman was sacked and replaced by Roy Hodgson, but the run did not quite end there. Palace went seven games without a goal or point.

Hodgson ultimately turned things around with Palace not only avoiding relegation, but remarkably finishing 11th. We are not suggesting Coventry sack their own Frank, by the way. He has surely earned enough goodwill after getting them into the top flight in the first place. Also, coaxing the 79-year-old Hodgson out of retirement could be tricky (but probably not impossible knowing him).

The other joint-longest run at the start of a Premier League season without a point belongs to Portsmouth, who failed to win their first seven in 2009-10. They did score three times in that run, but, unlike Palace, failed to improve much during the campaign. Pompey finished bottom on 19 points. They were deducted nine points for going into administration, but would have still finished bottom even without that.

Norwich lost their first six in the 2021-22 season and finished bottom on 22 points, while a further three teams have lost their first five in the Premier League: Southampton in 1998-99, Sunderland in 2005-06, and Wolves last season. Saints stayed up, but Sunderland and Wolves both disappeared to the Championship after finishing 20th.

Coventry are not the only team struggling. Things were supposed to be different for Tottenham. After back-to-back 17th-place finishes in the Premier League, Roberto De Zerbi kept them up by the skin of their teeth last season and the club backed him in the transfer window this summer. However, four games into the new campaign and, like Coventry, they are yet to score. They do at least have two points to their name after 0-0 draws against Nottingham Forest and Everton, but that familiar sinking feeling is already dousing pre-season optimism for Tottenham.

It is the first time in the club’s history they have failed to score in their first four league games of a campaign and, as mentioned, only that 2017-18 Palace side have endured a longer start to a Premier League season without scoring (seven games).

It has been 407 minutes since Spurs last scored in the Premier League and the first time they have failed to score in four successive Premier League matches since September 2006.

Apart from Spurs and Coventry this season, there have been five previous examples of teams failing to score in their first four Premier League games. As well as the aforementioned Palace campaign, there was Sheffield Wednesday in 1994-95, Newcastle in 2005-06, Swansea in 2011-12, and Aston Villa last season. Crucially, none of them were relegated with the lowest any of them finished 13th (Sheffield Wednesday).

That should provide plenty of hope for Spurs. Villa did not score until the fifth game last year, but went on to have a stellar campaign, finishing fourth and winning the Europa League. That said, their squad was badly hit by sales in the summer. Perhaps unsurprisingly, they have started slowly, one point from their first four games after a goalless draw at Hull. Defeats to Brighton, Arsenal and Forest have left them in the relegation zone, with a point fewer than they had this time last season.

It is the fourth time Villa have started a Premier League season without winning any of their first four games, after 1992-93, 1997-98, and 2025-26. At least they have scored, though, with Alysson’s equaliser against Forest on Saturday their first in the league. Again, though, Villa can use their marked improvement after this point last season as optimism fuel.

Fulham’s slow start was given a boost on Saturday with a well-earned draw at Liverpool, their first point of the season. Though they remain in the bottom three, they can build on that performance and silence those who had started to doubt them after opening with three defeats to Chelsea, Sunderland and Palace.

It’s four games down, 34 to go. Coventry will want their first points as soon as possible, while something as simple as scoring a goal could unlock Tottenham’s potential. There is plenty of time to restore positive vibes and have a great time between now and the end of May. Perhaps the teams who should be worried do not even know it yet.

This is an article by Opta Analyst

Sports.title: USA exits U-20 World Cup on penalties as tournament’s timing draws criticism
Sports.content:
The United States were eliminated from the U-20 Women’s World Cup in the last 16 on Wednesday, falling to Brazil on penalties after playing to a 1-1 draw after extra-time. Brazil goalkeeper Thaís Lima made a crucial save on Emeri Adames’s attempt to begin the shootout, opening the eventual 5-4 finish in Katowice, Poland.

The result extends a difficult run of form for US youth national teams across the men’s and women’s programs. This is the third time since last October that a US youth team has failed to win a knockout game at a World Cup: the U-17 boys and the U-17 girls both exited in the last 16 of their respective tournaments in shootouts. The U-20 men fell in the quarter-final of their World Cup in October 2025.

The US, holders of 2024 Olympic gold in women’s soccer and winners of two of the past three senior Women’s World Cups, last won the U-20 tournament in 2012, with a squad headlined by Crystal Dunn, Julie (Johnston) Ertz and Sam Mewis, all of whom are now retired.

In Poland, the Americans struggled to advance from their group, losing the opener against Italy before playing Japan to a 2-2 draw. A 9-0 rout of New Zealand was enough to reach the knockout round as one of the tournament’s top third-place sides. Brazil comfortably finished atop their group, beating Tanzania, Canada and England by a 9-2 aggregate.

While far from as testy as the senior national teams’ friendlies in June, the US and Brazil played a fairly scrappy game Wednesday. Brazil defender Sofia opened the scoring from a 59th-minute corner kick, while Seattle Reign midfielder Ainsley McCammon equalized from the run of play late in the 63rd. Neither team was able to find a breakthrough in the ensuing hour, leading to Lima’s heroics to open the shootout.

This is Brazil’s third straight quarter-final appearance at a U-20 Women’s World Cup, and seventh in 12 appearances. Their joint best finish was a pair of third-place showings in 2006 and 2022.

Emma Hayes ‘worried’ about tournament’s calendar

The timing of this year’s U-20 Women’s World Cup has drawn scrutiny from ex-players and coaches. Staged every other year, the tournament usually falls in either August or September, with this installment falling on the later end of the general timeframe. It is not being held in a Fifa window, so many in-season club teams opted not to release their players.

On Tuesday, a group of current and former players including Alex Morgan, Marta, Dunn and Sophia Wilson signed an open letter asking Fifa to reconsider the scheduling of its U-20 Women’s World Cups. Emma Hayes told ESPN that she was concerned about the mettle of US youth national teams, which have historically struggled in major tournaments and World Cups given the federation’s past approach to youth development that deprioritized competitions.

“When I speak about this subject, I am sending a warning sign that I am worried,” Hayes told ESPN. “I am massively worried about the direction for and the lack of all of those experiences for American players.”

A September tournament is complicated for players already signed to clubs regardless of how their league operates. For players in fall-to-spring seasons, like the Women’s Super League, it picks off young players fresh from club preseason, hampering their ability to work into the first team and overlapping with the start of their seasons. For other leagues on spring-to-fall timelines, like the NWSL, clubs are put in the position to accept or reject call-ups during an important point of the regular season.

Age-eligible US players who were absent from this tournament squad include OL Lyonnes midfielder Lily Yohannes, Bay midfielder Claire Hutton, rising center-back Jordyn Bugg and playmaking technician Melanie Barcenas.

North Korea are the defending champions of the tournament, which ends with the 27 September final.

Sports.title: Watching Cavan Sullivan, excitement is tempered by memories of hypetrains past
Sports.content:
The trouble with trying not to hype up Cavan Sullivan is that he keeps on doing cool stuff. Like this past weekend, when he scampers along on a Philadelphia Union breakaway, loses his man by stopping so suddenly it’s as if he’s pulled a ripcord, back-heels the cutback behind his standing leg, watches it slowly kiss off the far post and in, and celebrated the goal by bowing and doffing an imaginary top hat to the crowd.

Like when he doubles the score by setting up an attack and finishing it himself with a left-footed lash through the goalkeeper’s legs form an acute angle. Like when he fashions yet another goal by holding up the play and then suddenly springs a teammate up the right flank.

And that’s just this past weekend.

It’s hard not to get worked up when an American, two weeks and a day before his 17th birthday, almost matches Lionel Messi for goal involvements in Major League Soccer and the Leagues Cup since the World Cup. When he powers an entire team of grown men to a 10-game unbeaten run. When he breaks Freddy Adu’s record as the youngest Major League Soccer debutant by 13 days, at 14 years and 293 days old. When he has netted six goals and five assists in his last eight matches. When he appears to be on the eve of his first United States men’s national team call-up.

When his swagger and flair are vindicated by the advanced metrics, which suggest that he has already compiled the best MLS season ever by a teenager, outdoing Alphonso Davies. That he is, in fact, the league’s second-best American player right now.

What makes Cavan Sullivan so tantalizing is that he isn’t theoretical.

And yet we wince.

We have been down this road before. That way madness lies, let me shun that – so warned King Lear.

As an American soccer community, we have developed a reflexive recoil against the Godding up of yet another prodigy. Still, it’s hard to resist, even though we know better. From the experience of Bobby Convey, and Jamar Beasley, and John O’Brien, and Jozy Altidore, and Juan Agudelo, and Brek Shea, and Julian Green, and Gedion Zelalem. They had skills and bodies and brains we could dream on, which we never managed to resist.

Did you even remember Green and Zelalem? Green is 31 and presently without a club; Zelalem, now 29, plays for New Mexico United. Both were promised to us as potentially first American male superstar when they emerged from the Bayern Munich and Arsenal academies, respectively. But then, all the men on that list, and so many more, were supposed to be that. None of them were.

We’ve been doing this since the 1970s, when it was decided that Kyle Rote Jr, son of the gridiron football hero, would put soccer on the map. He did indeed become famous, but much less for what he did on a soccer field than for thrice winning the popular gameshow Superstars – wherein top players from different sports competed in a series of athletic events. He led the North American Soccer League in scoring as a rookie and then tailed off, taking a “sabbatical” to lead a hunger relief mission to Cambodia in 1980 and never playing soccer again.

They weren’t all failures. Several had solid professional careers. Altidore had a highly productive spell on the United States men’s national team – he is still its third all-time leading scorer, behind Landon Donovan and Clint Dempsey. His club resume, however, amounts to two good seasons in the Netherlands and half a dozen strong campaigns in Major League Soccer, after he had been discarded by five different European clubs.

There’s still no telling, exactly, what the now-23-year-old Gio Reyna might or might not become. His body hasn’t cooperated, breaking down again and again, and neither has he managed to muster the consistency to become a regular and productive starter on a European club (that may change this season with Strasbourg). He’s bounced around, largely anonymously, briefly resurfacing for World Cups. It feels like a long time ago now, when he was 17 and fit seamlessly into Borussia Dortmund’s attacking diamond with Erling Haaland, Jude Bellingham and Jadon Sancho.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Of all the chosen ones, only Christian Pulisic has really panned out something like we had hoped. He has, however, never really been the focal point in the attack of any of his three European clubs. And he’s developed an odd penchant for falling out of favor after two or three seasons, tumbling down the depth chart at Dortmund and then Chelsea and now Milan. Under new manager Ruben Amorim, Pulisic, the author of 52 goals and assists over the last three Serie A campaigns – albeit notably fewer of them in the 2025-26 season – has been benched and has appeared just once in the Italian league.

And all of them toiled under the looming specter of Adu. More than two decades on from Freddymania, his name is still invoked as a cautionary tale. He works as a personal skills coach now, and has done since last playing professionally five years ago.

So we proceed carefully, taking great pains not to make the same mistakes again.

The thing is, Sullivan has already scored more goals in two-thirds of an MLS campaign than Adu did in his highest-scoring season, his rookie year with DC United in 2004. And the league is a hell of a lot harder to score in these days. It’s better set up to handle transcendent talent, too.

Unlike most of the others, there are real numbers there. Real performances. Real highlight clips, captured at the senior level against credible opposition. Manchester City certainly think he’s real, long ago arranging for his transfer when he turns 18. It’s all there, other than the size of Sullivan himself. That may prove problematic. But then he wouldn’t be the first undersized superstar.

And yet.

Leander Schaerlaeckens is the author of The Long Game: US Men’s Soccer and Its Savage, Four-Decade Journey to the Top, or Thereabouts, which is out now. He teaches at Marist University.

Sports.title: JJ Gabriel could leave Man United in £300k deal but must abide by little-known rules to seal Real Madrid transfer
Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel could leave Man United in £300k deal but must abide by little-known rules to seal Real Madrid transfer

JJ Gabriel's dream move to Real Madrid could encounter a stumbling block due to FIFA rules on international transfers for under 18s.

The Manchester United wonderkid sent shockwaves on Tuesday when it was revealed that he had asked to leave Old Trafford.

3 Wonderkid Gabriel has dropped a bombshell and asked to leave Man United Credit: Getty

talkSPORT understands Real Madrid are now leading the race for Gabriel's signature but face competition from Barcelona and two Premier League clubs.

While the 15-year-old is being hotly pursued, his preferred destination is understood to be the Bernabeu.

Real Madrid complications

A departure from Old Trafford may well prove complicated for Gabriel, with several potential stumbling blocks emerging.

talkSPORT understands JJ Gabriel's family plan to relocate to Spain.

However, FIFA rules stipulate that if a player under age of 18 moves countries he must provide proof his family are moving to that country for 'non-footballing reasons'.

This could throw some doubt over his dream move to Madrid, even though his Irish passport could help his case.

Brexit rules mean English players must be 18 to join a team in Europe, unless they are a dual national with a EU country, subject to FIFA approval.

With Gabriel turning 16 on October 6, he had asked to leave the club ahead of his birthday next month, and his EU citizenship could be crucial in facilitating this.

However, there is no guarantee that FIFA will allow the move to happen, with previous cases being rejected.

In 2005, 16-year-old Paraguayan Carlos Javier Caballero's move to Cadiz in Spain was rejected.

3 Gabriel is viewed as a generational talent, and netted 23 times in 23 U18 Premier League fixtures last term Credit: Getty

The teenager's mum got a job at a restaurant in Spain but FIFA ruled the exception to article 19 - which prohibits the international transfers of Under 18s - was not valid as her finding employment was directly linked to his move.

FIFA rules aren't the only obstacle Gabriel faces, with Man United also able to reject his formal notice to cancel his registration with the club.

Should the Red Devils block his request, his next port of call would be to appeal to the Premier League.

Premier League rules state: “During your child’s registration period, their registration may only be cancelled if everyone agrees (the club, player and their parent/carer).

“If the parties don’t agree, then any person involved can also ask the Premier League to provide a binding decision on a termination request."

Meanwhile if Gabriel moves to an overseas club, United are expected to only receive around £300,000 in training compensation.

3 Gabriel spent pre-season with United's first team and was set to be in the squad for their Carabao Cup clash with Brighton Credit: Getty

Man United told to fight for Gabriel

In the wake of the bombshell news, the Red Devils have been urged to do all they can to keep hold of the youngster - who has been dubbed the 'kid Lionel Messi'.

talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook said on Tuesday's Breakfast Show: "I think optically it's a really bad look if Manchester United lose somebody who Ryan Giggs has gone on record as saying he's a generational talent

"Particularly if he was to join another English club, it probably tells you where United are at in terms of pulling power."

Gabriel was due to be named in United's matchday squad for their Carabao Cup third round clash against Brighton on Wednesday evening, live on talkSPORT.

But the latest developments have inevitably led to Gabriel not being involved.

He would have become United's youngest ever player, with former goalkeeper David Gaskell the incumbent record holder after he played his first game aged 16 years and 19 days.

Sports.title: Simon Jordan predicts Man City’s 115 charges saga could drag on ‘until end of the decade’
Sports.content:
Simon Jordan predicts Man City’s 115 charges saga could drag on ‘until end of the decade’

Simon Jordan thinks that Manchester City's 115 alleged financial breaches has potential to drag on for another FOUR years.

City have been accused of breaking 115 financial regulations, by the Premier League, with another 15 charges later added. The club has always denied any wrongdoing.



2 Man City's case was heard over two years ago, but we still appear no closer to finding a verdict Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

The actual hearing lasted 12 weeks and started two years ago today, but there is still no outcome.

And Jordan predicts a scenario where it drags on until the end of this decade.

Speaking on White and Jordan with Jim White and Danny Murphy, the former Crystal Palace owner shared his view on the ongoing wait for a verdict.



He said: "I said it would take a long time, it has taken a long time. It is their own fault.

"They shouldn't have gone for 115 charges. They should have picked five or six meaningful ones and delivered some consequences for Man City or exonerated them.



"If Man City find themselves at the wrong end of a verdict, it'll be the end of the decade before it's concluded.

"So, if it goes against Man City, it will be the end of the decade because they will bring an appeal.



"If it goes against the Premier League, the Premier League won't bring an appeal against it, even though, they were the ones who brought the action.

"It is what it is, and people are screaming from the rooftops about what Man City are doing, but Man City need to keep running their business.

"Everyone is questioning how they can spend £450million, but they didn't because they sold nearly £300million worth of players."

2 Jordan would like to see City publicly demanding an outcome because they insist they are innocent Credit: talkSPORT



State of play

Eight-time Premier League winners City are accused of breaching financial rules from 2009 to 2018.

The majority of the charges relate to not providing accurate financial information, not complying with UEFA's FFP and not revealing managerial compensation.

And 35 other charges are related to City not cooperating with the Premier League's investigation.

And Jordan believes that with City's stance insisting they are totally innocent, they should be demanding a resolution to the case.



"The Premier League clubs are paying for it," he added.

"If I am Man City, but I am waiting for two years to exonerate myself, I would be up in arms.

Man City's charges explained 1. Failure to provide accurate and up-to-date financial information from 2009-10 to 2017-18. 54 charges relating to breach 2. Failure to provide accurate financial reports for player and manager compensation from 2009-10 to 2017-18. 14 charges relating to breach 3. Failure to comply with UEFA's regulations, including UEFA's Club and Licensing and Financial Fair Play Regulations. Five charges relating to breach 4. Breaches of Premier League profitability and sustainability regulations from 2015-16 to and including 2017-18 season. Seven charges relating to breach 5. Failure to cooperate with Premier League investigations from December 2018-present 35 charges relating to breach

"I would be saying, 'where is this verdict? 'Because it is an absolute outrage that our name is being besmirched.'

"But it is strange that they are silent about it. I would have thought there would be more outrage.

"Surely, they must be infuriated. Why wouldn't they be shouting from the rooftops about where is the verdict."



Premier League's view

Man City were charged by the Premier League in February 2023, but there is still no outcome regarding the charges.

And speaking to talkSPORT in August, the Premier League's CEO Richard Masters was asked about the situation by our Chief Football Correspondent Alex Crook.

He said: "I obviously can't comment on it. I do understand the frustration. It has taken longer than expected, but we have to follow the process."

Crook then asked if it was damaging the Premier League, and Masters responded: "I hope not.



"In the end, the Premier League's responsibility is to ask the Independent Commission to look at serious allegations and to establish the truth.

"That shouldn't be qualified by it taking too long, for example."

Sports.title: Lionel Messi can extend record trophy haul and end MLS drought in newly-created fixture
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi has the chance to win his 48th career trophy on Wednesday night as Inter Miami eye a historic victory.

Messi currently holds the record for the most trophies ever won by a player, and he's now on the brink of extending it.



4 Messi has won 47 trophies across his career and now has the chance to extend his record with a 48th in the Campeones Cup Credit: AFP

The footballing legend will line up for Inter Miami in the Campeones Cup, which was only officially launched in 2018.

Mexican champions Cruz Azul will be their opponents, as the MLS winners and LIGA MX winners clash in the fixture.

The one-off match was created alongside the Leagues Cup - which is a tournament that includes clubs from the USA, Canada and Mexico - to help 'strengthen the sport in the region'.



Inter Miami have never played in the game before, meaning this is a chance for them to lift the trophy for the first time.

Their success in the MLS last season put them forward for the Campeones Cup and they will feel they need to beat Cruz Azul, not just for themselves or Messi, but for the league as a whole.



The American sides have lost to their Mexican opponents in every edition of the fixture since 2022.

LA Galaxy lost to Toluca last year, with Columbus Crew losing to Club America in 2024 and LAFC being beaten by Tigres in 2023.



Lionel Messi's record trophy haul

Messi is hoping to get his hands on his fourth trophy as an Inter Miami player at the $1billion Nu Stadium.

He has won 47 pieces of silverware across his iconic career, including four Champions Leagues and 10 La Liga titles.

The 39-year-old picked up those trophies with Barcelona, where he won 34 in total, while he also won Ligue 1 twice during his short stint with French giants Paris Saint-Germain.

4 Messi lifted the MLS Cup for Inter Miami last season, which qualified them for the Campeones Cup final against Cruz Azul Credit: Getty



Lionel Messi: Notable trophies won LaLiga : 10x (2004–05, 2005–06, 2008–09, 2009–10, 2010–11, 2012–13, 2014–15, 2015–16, 2017–18, 2018–19)

Champions League: 4x (2005–06, 2008–09, 2010–11, 2014–15)

Ligue 1: 2x (2021–22, 2022–23)

MLS Cup: 2025

Copa America: 2021, 2024

World Cup: 2022

On the international stage, Messi completed football by winning the World Cup with Argentina in 2022.

Either side of that incredible success, he led his country to Copa America glory, taking his tally to three international titles.

The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner, who has been nominated for the award again this year, is three clear of any other player when it comes to trophies won throughout his career.

His tally of 47 is three more than former Barcelona teammate Dani Alves, who won 44 and four more than PSG's Marquinhos, who has won 43 in his career so far.



And he sits a huge 12 titles clear of rival Cristiano Ronaldo, with the Portuguese icon lifting 35 trophies in total.

Messi can extend that gap with an Inter Miami victory against Cruz Azul, with the Campeones Cup clash taking place at 8pm local time on Wednesday night, which is 1am on Thursday in the UK.

4 Messi's World Cup win is sure to be the standout in his record-breaking collection of trophies, which beats Ronaldo's by 12 titles Credit: Getty

Campeones Cup past results 2018: Toronto FC 1-3 Tigres

2019: Atlanta United 3-2 Club America

2021: Columbus Crew 2-0 Cruz Azul

2022: New York City 2-0 Atlas

2023: LAFC 0-0 (2-4 on penalties) Tigres

2024: Columbus Crew 1-1 (4-5 on penalties) Club America

2025: LA Galaxy 2-3 Toluca

Who has won the Campeones Cup before?

As mentioned, MLS clubs haven't had the best luck in the Campeones Cup in recent years, with the Mexican sides dominating.



Toluca are the most recent winners, as they beat LA Galaxy 3-2 last year, with Club America succeeding in 2024.

They beat Columbus Crew on penalties - the same method that Tigres won the trophy over LAFC the year prior.

The last MLS team to win the Campeones Cup was New York City in 2022 amid early dominance from the Americans.

In the first four editions of the match, it was Atlanta United, Columbus Crew and New York City that came out on top.



So, can Inter Miami and new manager Kily Gonzalez join that exclusive group and bring the trophy back to the States?

4 Messi has a strong record against Mexican sides and he will hope to add another win on Wednesday Credit: Getty

What is Messi's record against Mexican teams?

Well, Messi's record against Mexican clubs certainly gives Inter Miami a good chance of getting their hands on the silverware.

He has played 10 times against Liga MX teams throughout his career in the USA and with Barcelona, losing just once.



The now-retired Argentina international has won five and drawn four in such outings across competitive games and friendlies.

For Miami, Messi has scored three goals in five clashes against teams from Mexico, including one against Cruz Azul.

Altogether, he's netted six times in his 10 such games.

Sports.title: Arsenal approached for perfect Max Dowman loan move by EFL club
Sports.content:
Luton Town have previously requested to take Max Dowman on loan from Arsenal, the club's senior scout has revealed.

The Hatters are managed by former Gunners midfielder Jack Wilshere.

4 Wilshere has tried to sign Dowman on loan for Luton multiple times, says Mick Harford Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Following Dowman's latest eye-catching display, it has been revealed Luton have tried to to sign the 16-year-old on multiple occasions.

The winger scored twice in a 4-2 win over Ipswich Town in the third round of the Carabao Cup on Tuesday night.

It has taken his tally to three goals in 14 first-team appearances for Arsenal since his debut in August 2025.

And Hatters head scout and club ambassador Mick Harford has lifted the lid on their interest in the teenager.

Luton eyed Dowman

He has revealed Wilshere spoke to Gunners boss Mikel Arteta about the possibility of taking Dowman on loan at Kenilworth Road.

When asked about Dowman on talkSPORT, Harford replied: "I think Jack's asked him a couple of times, Mikel, but I don't think he'll be going out on loan."

Dowman previously played under Wilshere for Arsenal's Under-18s during his time as manager.

He scored two goals and provided seven assists in 12 appearances under his fellow Hale End graduate.

The 34-year-old has been in charge of Luton since October having been handed his first senior managerial role.

Wilshere has since won 25 of his 51 matches in charge as well as lifting the EFL Trophy last season.

4 Dowman scored twice in Arsenal's win over Ipswich on Tuesday night Credit: Getty

Dowman and Wilshere compared

Harford has also compared Dowman's emergence to Wilshere's rise through the Arsenal academy.

The Hatters legend added: "Jack was a wonderful footballer, he still is on the training ground.

"He started, not as a wide man, but as a wide man tucking in those little pockets, getting on the ball and creating stuff.

"Dowman looks more of a wide man than a pocket player, but a wonderful talent.

"I think he will get more game time and I think if he produces, I think Arteta will play him.

"I'm a believer in if you're ready, I don't care what age you are. If you're good enough, you'll play and I'm sure he will. He looks like he's going to be a superstar."

4 Comparisons have been drawn between Dowman and a young Wilshere due to their wonderkid status Credit: PA:Press Association

Wilshere made his Arsenal debut aged 16 under Arsene Wenger back in 2008.

He went on to make 197 appearances for his boyhood club, scoring 14 goals and adding 28 assists from midfield.

The former England international also won two FA Cups with the Gunners as well as featuring 34 times for the Three Lions.

Following an injury-ravaged career, Wilshere retired from professional football aged 30 in 2022.

As well as his time at Arsenal, he also had permanent spells with West Ham, Bournemouth and Danish side Aarhus.

After retiring, Wilshere began his coaching career with the Gunners' Under-18s before spending the 2024/25 season at Norwich.

4 Wilshere has been in charge of Luton since October last year Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

During his time at Carrow Road he served as Johannes Hoff Thorup's assistant before a two-match spell as caretaker boss.

Having left the Canaries in May last year, Wilshere is less than a month away from celebrating 12 months as Luton boss.

The Hatters currently sit 12th in League One after six matches this season.

Under Wilshere, they ended last term in seventh, missing out on the play-offs by a single point.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi handed two month sack warning after ‘slightly embarrassing’ Liverpool defeat
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi has been warned the pressure could crank up on him if Tottenham Hotspur lose this weekend.

However, former Premier League midfielder Danny Murphy believes De Zerbi will not be sacked before November despite Spurs' winless start to the season.



3 De Zerbi has been warned he could come under pressure if Spurs lose to Aston Villa this weekend Credit: AFP

The north London outfit have taken just two points from their opening four Premier League matches without scoring a goal.

Meanwhile, Spurs were knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Liverpool on Tuesday night.

Murphy has labelled their 3-1 defeat at Anfield a 'little bit embarrassing' but still expects Spurs to finish in the top half this term.



De Zerbi's side host Aston Villa on Saturday, live on talkSPORT, in their final match before the international break.

Murphy backs De Zerbi

Another loss would not be enough for the Italian to be sacked, though, according to Murphy.



Instead, he expects the Spurs hierarchy to give him up to another two months once the club returns to action in October.

Speaking on White & Jordan, Murphy admitted: "They’ll climb up the table. I still think they’ll be in the top half.



"I am surprised how poorly they’ve started, but actually the turnover of players, a lot of new players have come in, some of them late. He’s not yet established his best 11.

"There’s a few decisions when you watch them play. I’ve done most of the games where it’s kind of a little bit baffling, but they’ve got enough.

"It’s just about getting through this initial bad spell. Last night didn’t help.

3 Murphy has labelled Spurs' defeat to Liverpool a 'little bit embarrasing' Credit: Shutterstock Editorial



"I think he picked a strong team, which he should have done because he’s under a bit of pressure.

"He’s got a lot of quality and competition for places, but he picked a really strong team and they played okay.

"They missed a couple of big chances in the first half which can change momentum in a game, but to lose 3-1 it’s a little embarrassing.

"There comes a point with every manager at every club where the fans will start and if they lose to Villa at the weekend before the international break, all of a sudden amazingly he’s under pressure.



"Even if they lose at the weekend, I still think they’ll give him a month or two after they get back from the international break."

What's next for Spurs?

Spurs face a three-week gap between matches after Saturday's 12:30pm kick-off against Villa due to the season's first international break.

3 De Zerbi's side are yet to score or win in the Premier League this season Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Following the match, their next fixture will be away to Manchester United on October 10.



Heading into the weekend, Spurs sit 17th in the Premier League after back-to-back goalless draws against Nottingham Forest and Everton.

Those results follow defeats to Brentford and Newcastle United to start the season.

De Zerbi was appointed Spurs manager in March on a five-year deal through to the summer of 2031.

Having guided the club to three wins from seven matches to end the season, he secured their top-flight survival on the final day of the campaign.



A home win over Everton saw Spurs finish two points clear of London rivals West Ham, who were relegated to the Championship.

Sports.title: Wrexham announce landmark milestone in £70m Racecourse Ground redevelopment
Sports.content:
Wrexham have completed the latest phase of their Racecourse Ground redevelopment project.

The Red Dragons are in the process of building a new 7,750-capacity Kop Stand.



3 Wrexham have completed the latest phase of their Racecourse Ground redevelopment Credit: Getty

Construction on the stand began in December, with the club hoping it will be completed ahead of the start of next season.

Their plans remain on course after the steelwork for the stand was completed.

Wrexham stadium milestone

Wrexham have announced the 125-tonne inverted ribbon truss has been successfully installed as part of the new stand's construction.



It has been described as 'one of the most technically complex’ engineering operations of the project.

Speaking to the club's media channels, Wrexham CEO Michael Williamson explained: "The successful lift and installation of the steel truss is a landmark moment for the club, not only in the construction of the new Kop Stand itself but also for the wider Gateway Project.



"We are now looking forward to seeing the Kop Stand continue to evolve and take shape over the coming months."

The construction of the new Kop Stand will restore the Racecourse Ground to a four-sided stadium.



It will also take the venue's total capacity over 18,000 and comply with UEFA category four requirements.

Reaching category four status would allow Wales to play home European Championship qualifiers and Nations League matches at the Racecourse Ground.

Wrexham at the Racecourse Ground

The venue was first built in 1807, but has been used for football since Wrexham began playing matches there in 1864.

3 Wrexham hope to complete the construction of the new Kop Stand ahead of next season Credit: Getty



At present, the Racecourse Ground has a capacity of 10,771 supporters.

However, that figure is set to reach over 18,500 once the new Kop Stand is completed.

The old stand was closed in 2008 due to concerns over fan safety.

It was subsequently demolished in 2023, leaving the ground with just three stands.

As a result, the stadium is the smallest by capacity in the Championship this season.



Wrexham are currently in their second successive season in the second tier.

3 Wrexham's ground will hold over 18,500 fans once the new stand is completed Credit: Shutterstock

Following three promotions in a row from the National League to the Championship, the club finished seventh last season.

Phil Parkinson's side currently sit 19th after seven matches this term following a 6-0 defeat to West Ham United last weekend.

Sports.title: Anthony Gordon warned teammate ready to take his place as Barcelona tipped to win LaLiga ‘by a mile’
Sports.content:
Anthony Gordon warned teammate ready to take his place as Barcelona tipped to win LaLiga ‘by a mile’

Andy Brassell believes Anthony Gordon cannot afford to rest on his laurels, even if Barcelona 'really needed him'.

Gordon joined from Newcastle before the World Cup and has quickly taken to life at Barcelona, registering five assists from his first six appearances.



3 Gordon has essentially replaced Marcus Rashford as Barcelona's left-winger Credit: Getty

But it's not just Gordon's attacking contributions that have made him so vital to Barca's early season success.

Anthony Gordon has been what Barca needed

"It's just the work he gets through off the ball," European football expert Brassell said on Monday's Hawksbee and Jacobs.

"He's ideal for them. They've really needed him because they weren't able to get Julian Alvarez, so they've been playing Raphinha as a centre-forward.



"Who knew, he's (Raphinha) absolutely brilliant at it."

Raphinha, who moved to Barcelona from Leeds in July 2022, has netted eight times in all competitions this season.

Previously a left-winger, the Brazilian's shift to centre-forward has proved transformative.



However, talkSPORT understands Raphinha is not seen as a long-term solution up front, with Harry Kane and Erling Haaland viewed as alternative targets should Barcelona fail to land Alvarez.

Which Barcelona teammate should Anthony Gordon be concerned about?

That could spell trouble for Gordon, who could be nudged down the pecking order if Raphinha is moved back to the left-wing.



But Raphinha isn't the only teammate Gordon has to worry about being usurped by.

"He's got good competition to keep him honest," Brassell said.

3 Raphinha has now scored over 80 goals for Barca since he moved from Leeds Credit: Getty

"Karim Adeyemi came on for him and scored the clinching goal near the end."

Like Gordon, Adeyemi moved to Barcelona in the summer.

However, Adeyemi, who joined from Borussia Dortmund, has started just twice for the Catalan outfit this term.



The 24-year-old started Barcelona's LaLiga opener where he got on the scoresheet in a 5-0 rout of Elche.

But since then, Adeyemi has been reduced to cameos ranging from 28 minutes to 10.

Even if Adeyemi is reduced to being Gordon's back-up on the left, at least for now, it still leaves Barcelona with a strong attacking option to call on when needed.

3 Adeyemi's goal against Levante was Barcelona's 21st from five LaLiga fixtures Credit: Getty



Brassell: Barcelona may be scoring for fun, but they won't win Champions League

And Brassell believes that spells bad news for the rest of the competition, as he claimed Barcelona will 'end up winning LaLiga by an absolute mile.'

Brassell's belief is backed up by Barcelona's blistering goalscoring rate, with Hansi Flick's side netting 26 goals in just six games across all competitions this term.

Should Barcelona maintain that rate and play 57 games, which was how many they played last season, they are on track to score an absurd 247 goals.

However, he's not-so-certain about their Champions League aspirations and pointed to their defence that has shown a worrying tendency to be too casual as the potential reason why.



"Defending like they are defending at the moment, they will not win the Champions League, I don't think," Brassell said.

"They're competitive, they can play anyone off the park, there's no doubt about that. They can score goals galore.

"Can they keep it out against top level opposition? That's the question."

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel reveals how Argentina's 'f*** it football' exposed England and left them 'waiting for death' - as he admits World Cup semi-final defeat left a 'scar' after late heartbreak
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel reveals how Argentina's 'f*** it football' exposed England and left them 'waiting for death' - as he admits World Cup semi-final defeat left a 'scar' after late heartbreak

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Thomas Tuchel has opened up on England's World Cup semi-final capitulation to Argentina and admitted he 'has to live with the scar' of the result.

The Three Lions had looked to be heading to their first World Cup final since 1966 when Anthony Gordon put them 1-0 ahead after 55 minutes.

However, Enzo Fernandez equalised in the 85th minute before Lautaro Martinez added an injury time winner in a gut-wrenching defeat which defined England's tournament.

A key point in the match came with 19 minutes to go when Tuchel subbed on Ezri Konsa and went to a back-five, before he later brought on fellow defenders Dan Burn and Nico O'Reilly.

From that moment on, Argentina dominated the game and Tuchel was heavily criticised, with many feeling his changes and in-game management cost England.

And, speaking on the FA's documentary about England's run called Reflections: England's World Cup Journey, Tuchel spoke about the 'agony of epic proportions' and pointed to Djed Spence's memorable sliding tackle to thwart an Argentina attack as a key moment.

Thomas Tuchel has opened up on England's World Cup semi-final capitulation to Argentina

England were 1-0 up but ended up losing 2-1 after Tuchel made a series of defensive changes

'It did something to me,' Tuchel told former England striker Daniel Sturridge. 'It did maybe something to the players, and we suddenly shifted into a mindset: "Let's just overcome it" - that's how we played.

'We played like there are four minutes left, but it was actually 30-40 minutes left to play. From execution, the details of execution, playing around in the deep build-up, playing around Messi, bringing them to one side, switching the side, bringing the game in the opponent's half, making them suffer, have time to recover physically and mentally in ball possession. We were lacking all these things.

'Argentina then played very, very quickly. Sorry for the language, "f*** it" football. "We have nothing to lose, so let’s f*** it."

'They played two wingers, two strikers, and Messi. So they just took a six off and put a 10 in. At some point they played 3-1-6. And we struggled.'

Tuchel also revealed why he decided to switch to a back-five, having deployed the strategy in successful knockout victories over Mexico and Norway.

He added: 'A key moment, if I think about what happened to my decision-making, we conceded a big, big chance right before the water break.

'And I thought, "Okay, we will not survive. This is waiting for death." We don't have ball possession. We're not defending good. We're not defending properly in our 4-4-2. We need help.

'Coming with this mindset and coming with the experience that we ended the game against Norway in a back-five, we ended the match against Mexico in a back-five, and we did it.

'I thought they [Argentina] rely heavily on crosses. They have four strikers in the last line. I thought like, "Okay, let's play a back five here."

Tuchel reflected on his decision-making and insisted he 'has to live with the scar' of the loss

Tuchel insisted that 'no one knows what would've happened' if he deployed different in-game tactics, and defended his changes as he added: 'We could have done it and maybe lost 2-1 and people would go like: "Is he crazy? Against Norway, he finished the game with five. Why not finish the game off with five?"

'I think from what I saw and the experience and the information and the level of craziness that Argentina put in, change after change after change, it was one offensive change after the other, that was just my solution to the problem.

'I tried to help, that’s what the intervention of a coach is. I tried to help. You don't try to implement anything for your ego or whatever. You just try to help.

'If we would have been more stable in the game, let's say with more percentage of ball possession, I would have not changed the structure - why would I? And I would've gone for offensive changes.'

The German coach continued: 'But that is a very, very difficult road to go down that can torture you and you can try to kill me here, but it's my scar. It's not your scar. I have to live with it. You don't have to live with it. I have to live with this.

'I am in charge here, and I take these decisions. It's the players' scar, and it's my scar, and I have to live with it and keep on going.

'No one is more hurt than me. No one wanted it more. And you can now endlessly torture yourself and think if I would have done a different substitution, then we would've won the match. You just don’t know it.'

England are back in action later this month when they kick off their Nations League campaign with two fixtures against Czech Republic and one against Spain and Croatia.

Tuchel will name his squad for that international camp on Friday morning.

Sports.title: Man United academy star aims cryptic swipe at JJ Gabriel after teenager's quit threat - as teenager wipes ALL mention of Red Devils from his Instagram account
Sports.content:
Manchester United fans have been left stunned after youngster Shea Lacey seemingly aimed a cryptic swipe at wantaway starlet JJ Gabriel. United were rocked on Tuesday when it emerged that 15-year-old Gabriel, the jewel of their academy, wanted to leave. The incipient talent, dubbed 'kid Messi', left the hierarchy shocked with his request and it is understood that he has been dropped for today's Carabao Cup match against Brighton. And last night, Lacey appeared to stick the boot in with a viral post which has whipped up strong emotions among the fanbase. Lacey, 19, simply shared a picture of him arriving at Old Trafford and a love heart emoji in a post which has now been viewed 5.9 million times. United supporters came out in mass support in the comments, telling him 'you are the future' and 'you chose to stay at United, that's real passion my boy'. Shea Lacey posted this cryptic tweet after the news that JJ Gabriel wants to leave Man United Gabriel, 15, is considered one of English football's best talents but now wants to leave By contrast, Gabriel's social media conduct has not endeared him to supporters after he wiped all reference to the club from his Instagram account. It should be stressed that Gabriel is not fully accountable for his decision and image – like any player, he will have a family and agency team behind him who are heavily influential. Daily Mail Sport's Oliver Holt has pinned the blame for his would-be exit on the club, asking why English football's hottest youth property would entrust his future to an institution in decline with controversial owners. Less than a week ago, Gabriel scored a hat-trick on his UEFA League debut against FK Sabah, becoming the youngest player in United history to do so. Last summer, when Gabriel flirted with an exit, director of football Jason Wilcox intervened. Along with head of negotiations Matt Hargreaves, he convinced Gabriel of his route to becoming the youngest-ever first-team player. This season, Gabriel has been playing six years up and is thriving with the under-21s. United sources believe there is still the possibility that the situation can be rectified given that despite the player’s request, he cannot be de-registered from the squad and his current contract runs until the end of the season. Eyebrows were raised when it appeared Gabriel had wiped his Instagram account of all its photos and took out all mentions of Manchester United. Gabriel, nicknamed 'Kid Messi', scored a hat-trick in the UEFA Youth League last week Sources close to the player were quick to play down talk of discontent but it has now transpired that an explosive episode has been brewing behind the scenes, with Barcelona having spent years pursuing him, given he can leave the UK at 16 due to holding an Irish passport, allowing him to play in Europe. Only days ago after scoring the European hat-trick Gabriel’s boss at youth level Adam Lawrence, who leads the Under-19s and the Under-21s, spoke about coaching a player like Gabriel. ‘I think the first thing in my job is not to ruin him,’ Lawrence said. ‘So when you have a talented player like JJ and the other lads of course, you obviously don't want to stifle their freedom and their creativity. And I think essentially what you try and do is to set the team up to allow the talent to function and to play free at the right moments. ‘Of course, it can't always be free and off the cuff in terms of some of the off-the-ball responsibilities that he's working on and some of the pressing things that he's thinking about. But again, in terms of how he plays properly and how he connects with other team-mates at the top end of the pitch, he's just in a real good space. ‘If you look at that game today, I think he's playing properly. I think he's trying to do the right things. ‘It's enjoyable working with him and challenging as a coach because the best players challenge you. When you work with talented players you have to find a way to help them and allow them to flourish and keep improving. Of course, there are things that you can keep working on but he is of course in a real good place.’ Asked about the people advising him, Lawrence was insistent those around him have the player’s best interests at heart. The move has left United shocked and is a significant blow given how highly rated Gabriel is ‘With JJ, he's surrounded by people that really believe in him,’ Lawrence added. ‘From the top of the club right the way through. Where he's been at the club for so long, he's got good relationships with the players, with the staff. ‘Over the course of time that helps as well. At the moment just in terms of his game, his games programme, his training programme, making sure that he's getting the right exposure across different levels. ‘We're obviously not perfect but it's definitely something we put a lot of thought into. So yeah, it's good to see him just enjoying his football and in a good place for sure.’ But those comments come as scant consolation to supporters now with Gabriel determined to seek pastures new, particularly when a first team debut had long been earmarked for this week.

Sports.title: Anthony Elanga's likely return date as club insiders sweat on injury, Toon's transfer plan at centre back and Matthias Jaissle's 'naivety' at Leeds: Newcastle Confidential Q&A Special
Sports.content:
Anthony Elanga's likely return date as club insiders sweat on injury, Toon's transfer plan at centre back and Matthias Jaissle's 'naivety' at Leeds: Newcastle Confidential Q&A Special

Newcastle’s bruising defeat at Leeds has raised questions over Matthias Jaissle’s tactics and the make-up of his squad.

So, what happens next – and how worried should supporters be?

In our latest Newcastle Confidential Q&A special, CRAIG HOPE answers your questions on Anthony Elanga’s injury, Nico Gonzalez’s concussion and Joelinton’s recovery.

He also reveals the club’s plans at centre back, examines why Newcastle are being overrun in midfield and asks whether Jaissle has built a system around a No 10 he does not actually have...

Any news on Anthony Elanga’s injury?

This cannot be definitive, because another scan is scheduled, but my information coming out of Leeds was of a muscle injury in the hamstring area that would keep Elanga sidelined for around six-to-eight weeks.

I know those inside the club are concerned about the gravity of the problem, but only when another MRI scan is complete will they communicate the full prognosis. Those tests, I’m told, are taking place this week.

Either way, Elanga is facing a period in the treatment room. The problem, say sources, is not knee related, despite speculation.

Anthony Elanga is facing an extended spell on the sidelines - though he doesn't have a knee injury, despite speculation to the contrary

Will Nico Gonzalez get the all-clear to play on Saturday? (Saeb Macafi)

No. There is a loophole that allows a player to return if they were only taken off with ‘suspected concussion’, but even then the earliest point of clearance is seven days.

My sources say the team are preparing for the weekend on the assumption Gonzalez will not be involved.

What's the situation with Big Joe? (Clare Bremmer)

Joelinton has a quad injury that is not as bad as first feared, at least in that it does not require surgery.

However, by the time he returns after the international break, his absence would have extended to two months, and that is assuming there are no setbacks.

In other news, I’m hearing Bruno Guimaraes had a sleepover at Joelinton’s place following his goal against Sunderland at the weekend, although I suspect their customary kickabout in the back garden had to be sacrificed.

Former Newcastle star Bruno Guimaraes (left) stayed over at Joelinton's house following Arsenal's win at Sunderland

Could Will Osula be the answer on the right wing? (Bobby Martins)

First of all, Osula needs to get fit. His foot injury is said to be healing well and he should be in contention for the trip to Coventry on October 12.

In theory, as last season’s brilliant goal against Manchester United showed, he is dangerous cutting in from the right. But Osula is a central striker and thrives playing on the shoulder of centre backs. I’m not sure he’s cut out for a more disciplined role with responsibility to work both ways.

One of the reasons Jaissle doesn’t yet fancy Bazoumana Toure as a starter, I’m told, is his need to work on the defensive side of his game as a winger.

Why did we invest so much in midfielders but not in centre halves? I was pointing out all summer how vulnerable we were in that position with ageing and injury-prone players. Does Jaissle want to invest in a CB in January and how do we cope till then? (Shearer’s Slipper)

Centre backs were put to the club by agents early in the window and the likes of Fikayo Tomori were closely monitored. But once a new deal for Fabian Schar was agreed, the plan was always to stick with him, Sven Botman, Malick Thiaw and Dan Burn. Staff have also spoken about Amar Dedic being able to play in the middle.

The problem Newcastle had in this position, when it came to the summer market, was that they needed to trade one out to bring one in. Botman had not long signed a new contract; Burn is 34, club captain and settled, while Thiaw has been at the club only one season and is not a player they want to sell.

As for Jaissle, he will be assessing what he has and doesn’t have all of the time. But a club like Newcastle, in an SCR world, can’t really afford to carry more than four senior centre backs.

The longer-term plan is to replace Schar, 34, next summer with a centre back in the 21-to-24 age profile. However, the performance of the other three this season – especially if they struggle – could see more drastic change in an area of the pitch in which, I agree, Newcastle suddenly look vulnerable.

Newcastle plan to replace 34-year-old Fabian Schar (left) with a younger centre back next summer

Do you think the team were prepared correctly for the Leeds game? It felt like there was a failure in the overall game plan, but more worryingly in the basic preparation of patterns, marking and motivation (Sean Brown)

Well, I’ve heard nothing to suggest they weren’t prepared (under some former managers I was often told that they weren’t!) and all of the noise around Jaissle has been positive. But what played out in front of us at Elland Road did look void of the elements you mention.

One word that has been put to me by those close to the club in recent days is ‘naive’. That in the sense of Newcastle playing a 4-2-4, in effect, against a Leeds side who crowd the middle of the park.

Such naivety is, of course, all part of the learning curve for a new manager in a new country.

But the first half on Monday night was as bad a 45 minutes as I can remember post-takeover – and that was simply because of the absence of the basic application you would expect when it comes to tackling, marking and running.

That should be a concern because, as Jaissle said, those are the ‘non-negotiables’.

Matthias Jaissle will have been furious with what he saw at Elland Road on Monday night, as his players failed at basics like tracking back, marking and tackling

Do we still need a top No 9, rather than a 10? (John Keith)

I would argue they still need both! But the bigger issue is the No 10, especially if Jaissle continues to use one. Because, for me, he does not have a No 10!

Yoane Wissa is a No 9 and does not have the qualities a player in the deeper position needs – that is not his fault, it’s just not him.

Joe Willock can do a job there, but it’s not his position. The same for Jacob Ramsey. Matias Fernandez-Pardo has told the club he wants to play centre forward.

So, there you go – a team built around a No 10 when it doesn’t really have one. They need someone who can act as an extension of the midfield, who can control the tempo of a game and open doors. At present, the players used are out-of-position runners.

Wissa can have a good season, I really believe that, but only as a central striker.

Yoane Wissa (pictured celebrating his goal at Tottenham last month) has made a bright start to the season but isn't the answer at No 10

Eddie Howe got it in the neck about not being tactically flexible, so we have to be consistent with Jaissle – why is he sacrificing his midfield to play Wissa as a 10? Wissa is a striker and we're being overwhelmed in midfield. Every opponent will run and pass through us just like with Howe (Pablo Hopez)

Is Jaissle tactically flexible enough to accept we are light in midfield and need extra bodies? Ruben Amorim made that mistake at Man Utd (Geoff Adamson)

Is Jaissle dead set on having only two in midfield after we have had two Premier League games in a row now and been completely overrun? (Smithy)

Jaissle’s preferred system is 4-2-3-1, for sure – he has told us that. But only he can answer the questions you pose with his team selection.

As you all say, there is an issue in midfield that needs to be addressed. I flagged it before the trip to Leeds and my suspicion of them being overrun played out.

The problem Jaissle has this weekend against Hull is that Gonzalez, Joelinton and Ramsey are all likely to be missing. Maybe a three of Lewis Miley, Sean Steur and Joe Willock would be the best bet for this game. To go with two in midfield would perhaps lay a blueprint for Hull to exploit.

Right now, Miley and Steur between them don’t have the physicality needed for a Premier League midfield pairing. Miley, in mitigation, looks like he needs a good run of games to build fitness, rhythm and confidence.

Midfielder Lewis Miley looks like he needs a good run of games to build fitness, rhythm and confidence

Do you think we will be relegated based on what you have seen so far? (Daniel Hickey)

No. But I did say at the start of the season that a repeat of 12th would probably represent a decent campaign based on how the summer played out, even though they salvaged the window with some good business towards the end.

I know the ambition internally is European football, and after a few games there was optimism in that regard, but my realistic take has always been that this year will likely be a bottom-half finish.

What is the highest finish the club would still consider a disaster this season? (Kizza)

Well, the hierarchy have labelled 12th a ‘disappointing end’ to last season, and they say that within the context of each position lost or gained equating to £2.6million in prize money.

So, to answer the question, I’d say anything below 12th would be disappointing for them. A ‘disaster’ would be relegation.

How do they expect to meet this 2030 target (of being the best in the world) if they are routinely selling our best players and stubbornly holding on to the likes of Murphy/Willock when we get perfectly good offers for them? (Capitao39)

It’s a question a lot of supporters are asking re the non-sales of Jacob Murphy and Willock. In defence of Murphy, Jaissle really wanted to keep him and I understand why. He values his leadership in a young dressing room.

Also, the final £15m offer from Nottingham Forest landed on deadline day, so it was too late to replace him. The original offer of around £10m did come a week or so earlier.

Some Newcastle fans wanted to see Joe Willock (left) and Jacob Murphy sold this summer, but Willock has started the season well and Murphy is an important leader in the dressing room

As for Willock, I agree with your point. The club could have negotiated his sale sooner in the window and reinvested. Saying that, Willock has started the season well and will probably emerge as an important player in the coming weeks. He’s got the legs that others haven’t.

The club also felt the turnover of players was already very high and were conscious of having some continuity and stability.

As for where all of this leaves Vision 2030… I’m on the record in saying that, while I admire the ambition, I’m not sure it is deliverable in four years. I believe the hierarchy are well-intended, competent and will push as hard as they can, but I don’t see a club (on the pitch or off it) that feels on the coattails of the top six at present.

Sports.title: Chelsea suffer huge blow as Joao Pedro is forced to withdraw from Brazil squad through injury just two days before Brentford clash
Sports.content:
Joao Pedro has been forced to pull out of the Brazil squad for the upcoming international break because of injury, in what could be a blow to Chelsea before their Friday night trip to Brentford. The 24-year-old striker has scored three goals and assisted three in the Premier League this season at the head of a front three including Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers. Joao Pedro’s problem and whether it is major or minor has not been disclosed. Brazil cited an 'injury' as the reason for his withdrawal as they called up Matheus Martinelli in his place. Chelsea declined to comment when contacted, though Xabi Alonso will be asked about his striker at his pre-Brentford press conference at 1.30pm on Thursday. Chelsea fans will be hoping to hear his withdrawal is purely precautionary, though pulling out of Brazil duty will have them concerned that he is unlikely to feature this Friday at least. The Blues have not won at the Brentford Community Stadium since 2021. Chelsea star Joao Pedro has withdrawn from the upcoming Brazil squad due to injury The striker is yet to score for Brazil and was a shock omission from their World Cup squad Without Joao Pedro, Danny Welbeck, the 35-year-old signed from Brighton in the summer, would likely lead their front line. There was some concern earlier this week when Chelsea trained at Cobham and the first 15 minutes were made publicly available. Joao Pedro was not involved in those early stages of the session, along with Reece James and Moises Caicedo, who has been nursing a calf issue. Joao Pedro was due to return to the Brazil squad after being snubbed for the World Cup by manager Carlo Ancelotti, who has been in attendance at Chelsea games this season. They are scheduled to play games against Australia and India during the break, with significant travelling involved for those who play in England, including Chelsea starlet Estevao. After facing Brentford this Friday, Chelsea are not due to play again until Bournemouth visit on Saturday October 10 after a three-week break.
