Sports.title: Battle of boxing's most unlikeable stars: Conor Benn takes on troubled Ryan Garcia after burning Eddie Hearn with $10MILLION payday in his sights - but here's why Briton's fate rests solely in the hands of his narcissistic American rival
Sports.content:
Battle of boxing's most unlikeable stars: Conor Benn takes on troubled Ryan Garcia after burning Eddie Hearn with $10MILLION payday in his sights - but here's why Briton's fate rests solely in the hands of his narcissistic American rival

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

‘Who ya like buddy?’ It’s the most asked question in casino-ville as the hours tick down to this Saturday’s world title fight between two angry young men.

One, America’s extravagantly gifted but troubled world welterweight champion. The other, the ever-persistent English challenger who never stops throwing punches whether they connect or not. As if in manic obsession with defeating not only opponents but also his demons and a sceptical outside world.

So, Ryan Garcia or Conor Benn?

When the denizens of this neon gambling Strip in the Nevada desert ask that question they don’t’ want to know which of these two combatants you like personally more than the other. It is their way of trying to find out who you might be betting on to prevail in the atmospheric T-Mobile Arena.

Their inquiries are even more numerous than usual on such occasions as this. Because neither the Americans nor the Mexicans who are thronging here in support of their blood brother by heredity know very much about Benn. Other than the fact he is the son of a fabled icon of the British ring.

On his two previous US visits Benn Jr made hard work of beating men who looked more like nightclub bouncers than professional boxers. Of his exploits back home only the pair of fights against Chris Eubank Jr evoked any interest whatsoever on either side of this border.

What they are aware of is the two positive tests for performance enhancing drugs and the protracted legal battle to technically clear his name which kept him out of the ring for months. Just as they know about Garcia’s conviction and suspension for a similar finding.

Conor Benn is locked in the battle of boxing's most unlikeable stars in Las Vegas

Benn is lining up a $10m payday after burning his bridges with promoter Eddie Hearn

So, what’s to like?

There can be no doubting Benn’s work ethic. He trains like a dervish to manufacture the maximum possible out of however much natural-born ability he inherited from Nigel the Dark Destroyer. Nor does he ever give up. Eubank Jr had to go beyond the normal limits of even this battle-hardened business to inflict the only defeat of Conor’s career thus far. A loss he avenged, albeit in partly contrived and contentious circumstances.

Eubank the Younger was perilously drained in the rematch by a clause in the contract which prevented him rehydrating fully after struggling to cut poundage to meet the agreed catchweight.

What goes around comes around. If not in a full measure of the irony. Benn has had to sweat and strain down by almost a stone from middleweight to make the welterweight championship limit of 147 lbs. As he puts it: ‘Five weeks in hell.’

To say his body looks shredded is putting it mildly. But he has not been subjected to rehydration limitations following his Friday morning visit to the scales.

Eubank was handsomely rewarded to put his health on the line, and now Benn has been lured into similar jeopardy by the fortune – some reports say ten million dollars – he is receiving from UFC boss Dana White to be one of the first poster boys for his venture into boxing.

Benn tells it otherwise: ‘I’m doing this because I relish challenges. Have always wanted to strap on the same green WBC belt my dad was so proud to wear. To start getting the world titles that will leave a legacy for my kids. And to prove wrong everyone who doesn’t give me a chance of winning. That puts all the pressure on him, not me.’

Hearn backed the British fighter during his controversial doping ban saga

Ryan Garcia stands in his way of the WBC title, who is the more talented of the fighters

WEIGH-IN VERDICT: After all the brouhaha Conor Benn made the weight with a full pound to spare After what he described as 'five weeks of hell' dieting down by two divisions he scaled 146 lbs in readiness to challenge world welterweight champion Ryan Garcia here this Saturday night. He did so with a told-you so smile. Throughout the speculation as to whether he could shed the best part of a stone in his training camp journey from middleweight Benn had assured one and all that he would be comfortable at his long-ago weight. Good as his word he came in only half a pound heavier than Garcia. Although he is leaner of hip the muscle is still there on arms and torso. Complete with a six pack as a reminder of his constant work ethic. The slightly taller part/Mexican great white hope of American boxing does look more natural at the weight. But Benn does not appear stressed from all his exertions. Even so Garcia is still a solid odds on favourite in the Vegas betting

Whether or not Benn can take in sufficient liquids and pasta before entering the ring, the dangers to him are greater than those with which Eubank struggled. Garcia, one year the younger at 28 but the riper in championships experience, has authentic one-hit-knockout power.

Benn goes into his first world championship fight reliant on the cumulative effect of his non-stop output. The problem with this is that King Ry is probably the best counterpuncher in the world right now and Benn’s headlong style will likely suit him nicely, thank you.

To complicate the evaluation, both have blotted their copybooks as people. Garcia, the handsome heartthrob, burnished his bad-boy rock-star image by trashing a five-star hotel room. He also needed his family’s help with overcoming mental problems aggravated by a passing fancy for social drugs and booze.

Benn invited mockery for claiming initially that he failed his drugs tests because of eating enough eggs to fill the shelves of all the Tescos in London. Then, in order to collect his bonanza from Mister UFC, he unceremoniously dumped his long-time promoter Eddie Hearn who had bankrolled his hefty legal costs and loaned him half a million quid to help sustain his flamboyant lifestyle through that crisis.

Not much to like there.

So, when it comes to the fight, who ya like? The answer is not Conor Benn’s to give. Because the real question is which Ryan Garcia turns up.

If it is the narcissist whose arrogant complacency has cost him a couple of big fights, it may not be totally beyond the bounds of possibility that Conor could pull off one of the major upsets by a British boxer abroad.

If it is King Ry fully prepared and ready to unfurl all the majesty then we can only hope the son of Nigel is not seriously hurt.

Sports.title: Ricky Hatton's mother recalls last hug with boxing champion three days before he took his own life a year ago as parents speak out for first time
Sports.content:
Ricky Hatton's mother has recalled her last hug with him three days before he took his own life one year ago as his parents speak out for the first time.

Carol and Ray Hatton have urged people to tell their friends and family they love them before it's too late after the boxing champion hanged himself on September 14 last year.

One year on from Ricky's death, aged 46, his mother has revealed the last time she embraced her son.

Just days before he took his own life, the boxing champion had been in an argument with his parents but the family were 'building bridges'.

Carol decided to make an unplanned visit to his gym in Hyde and gave him a 'real proper hug'.

She told ITV News: 'I pulled up on the car park because I saw his car. He asked if everything was okay.

'I said "yeah, everything's fine". I said I'd like to see a bit more of him.'

Ricky's mother said he told her he wanted to see his father Ray the next week. However Ricky died three days later.

Former world boxing champion Ricky Hatton died by suicide in September last year aged 46

Ray and Carol Hatton (pictured at their son's funeral) have urged people to tell their friends and family they love them before it's too late

Ricky had previously opened up about his struggle with drug and alcohol addiction and had become estranged from his parents before the reconciled

She added: 'I'm so glad (I got to see him) because nobody knows when it's the last time you're going to see somebody.'

Ray, the boxer's father, said: 'You tell your grandkids how much you love them, you tell your wife how much you love them but I think, especially with men, don't ever be afraid of getting hold of your son and telling him you love him.'

Ricky had become estranged from his parents for around a decade before he reached out to patch up their relationship several years before his death.

He had survived previous suicide attempts and struggled with drug and alcohol addiction.

Ricky fell out with his parents over money and despite the dispute he still allowed Carol and Ray to see his newborn daughter Millie.

However the boxer became upset when his girlfriend Jennifer was not invited to a Christmas Day party.

Months later he received letters from his parents' lawyers saying they wanted to see their granddaughter.

But he told Manchester Evening News in 2013 that he responded by saying: 'I replied to my parents, through solicitors, and said we did not want them to have contact with Millie.'

Carol Hatton wipes a tear from her eye while reading a statement at her home after Ricky's death

Ricky had survived previous suicide attempts before he died in September last year

'We have never stopped them seeing her, as far as I was concerned they had just not been ******.

'I know that sounds harsh and I am sure they see it differently, but it is how I feel.'

He added that the situation 'was a mess', describing the family feud as 'bitter and horrible', referring to back-and-forth letters between his and his parents' lawyers.

This culminated in his father attacking him in a car park fist fight.

Angry about 'all that stuff you've written about your mum in that solicitor's letter', Ray then punched his boxing champion son in the face before Ricky hit back and his father then drove off.

But Ricky's parents are still struggling to come to terms with his death and Carol said the couple 'have to move forward' but will continue 'remembering him and loving him'.

Carol and Ray have now called for a statue of Ricky to be erected in Manchester, saying it would be a 'fitting tribute' to their son who 'brought a lot of pride' to the city.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury looks set for CARDIFF - at 2am: Welsh venue set to waive curfew to take boxing's biggest fight away from Wembley and New York
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury looks set for CARDIFF - at 2am: Welsh venue set to waive curfew to take boxing's biggest fight away from Wembley and New York

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Cardiff's Principality Stadium now looks set to be the unlikely winner of the venue war for boxing's biggest fight - by hosting Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury in the early hours of the morning.

The local authorities could today approve lifting the stadium's 10.30pm curfew to host the fight - stepping in after rows over holding it at Wembley Stadium or Madison Square Garden in New York.

Cardiff has history of hosting late-night boxing. Joe Calzaghe fought Mikkel Kessler at the Principality in 2007 at 2am. Fury and Joshua could fight at a similar time to satisfy broadcaster Netflix's huge audience in the United States.

Netflix had wanted the fight in New York to suit their prime timezones, while Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn pitched Wembley to host under the guise that Britain's biggest fight of the century should be hosted in the UK - and he has refused to budge unless contracts are rewritten with upgraded financial offerings.

Cardiff now appears to be the compromise. The Principality Stadium has an 80,000 capacity and a retractable roof - unlike Wembley - which could be useful in late November or December. A date of Saturday, November 28 has been mooted.

The Times report a press conference is tentatively scheduled for next week pending the approval.

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua could now be set to fight in Cardiff, Wales in November

Joshua and his camp wanted the fight in the UK - while broadcasters Netflix wanted a US host

Wembley looked an ideal venue for the fight but the strict 11pm curfew has been a sticking point, despite London mayor Sadiq Khan saying he wanted to ensure allowances were made to host the fight.

Boxing dealmaker Turki Al-Sheikh has been insistent on a start time of 2am.

Netflix have been running s for Fury-Joshua as recently as Thursday night, clearly confident an agreement will be struck.

The streaming giant has yet to sign off on Cardiff but American sportswriter Dan Rafael last night reported he had asked Netflix if they would approve, with a source telling him: 'I think they're OK.'

A spokesperson for the Welsh Rugby Union said: 'We'd be delighted to host this fight.

'We are very keen to attract more boxing to the stadium, which has a rich history in the sport, enhanced by its closable roof, unrivalled sight lines and unique city-centre location.'

Joe Calzaghe trains at the Principality Stadium before his 2am fight there in 2007

Joshua has fought in Cardiff twice previously, beating Carlos Takam and Joseph Parker in the Welsh capital in 2017 and 2018.

While Joshua has left Hearn to do the talking on his side of the deal, Fury has been publicly speaking and threatening that the heavyweight contest will be called off.

This week he suggested he will no longer be fighting Joshua in another social media rant as rows over the location and contract surrounding the fight continued.

'So it looks like AJ has s*** his pants yet again,' Fury said on social media on Sunday. 'After 11 years, he's finally s*** his pants yet again.'

Last week, Fury, who regularly takes to social media to express his views on potential opponents, was keen to make clear he feels Joshua is not motivated by a love of his country. Earlier this year Daily Mail Sport revealed Joshua had in fact quit the UK to move to Dubai – even as thousands tried to flee amid rising panic in the Middle East warzone.

And Fury, a tax exile to the Isle of Man himself, brought up a 2020 speech at a Black Lives Matter march, where Joshua read out a letter from his friend Reece Campbell to urge attendees to stop spending money with white-owned shops and businesses.

'Show them where it hurts', Joshua had said. 'Abstain from spending your money in their shops and economies, and invest in black-owned businesses.'

Fury re-posted the video of the speech, writing: 'This is the man who loves England, absolute s*** bag! Total piece of s*** bully with zero guts! Don't let them deceive you! & Living in Dubai.'

Provided Cardiff hits no further stumbling blocks, the Welsh capital may now offer the solution to get the fight on at last.

Sports.title: Bruising F1 2026 will not be the end for Russell - Wolff
Sports.content:
Toto Wolff is confident that George Russell can overcome a bruising 2026 Formula 1 campaign and still become world champion in the future.

The Mercedes driver is second and 81 points behind his dominant team-mate Kimi Antonelli with just nine rounds remaining, meaning a maiden crown for the 20-year-old is a matter of time.

It comes despite Russell entering 2026 as the heavy title favourite as he maximised the W16 last year with fourth in the standings and 169 points ahead of seventh-placed Antonelli.

Very few expected Antonelli to make such a strong leap into his sophomore season after a very up-and-down rookie campaign, but he is the one to have capitalised upon the rocket ship Mercedes has delivered for 2026.

“You can have good races, bad races, good years and bad years, but we're talking about the driver that has won everything that you could have potentially won before,” said Wolff of Russell at the Spanish Grand Prix.

“Every single karting championship, Formula 3 in his rookie year, Formula 2 in his rookie year, went into the Williams. We're talking about the top driver.

“We need to find out what is it for him to be able to unleash that potential and of course, there's the psychological side. If you have a run like him this year, you're taking a beating.

“But the great ones, they recover. And I think that George has all it needs to fight for championships and even if that one has maybe sailed, there will be more.”

George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Rudy Carezzevoli / Getty Images

The Spanish Grand Prix was where Antonelli took his second consecutive victory after Monza, which was particularly damaging for Russell as the Italian started 19th with his team-mate on the front row.

It has all led to Russell effectively conceding that “I don’t think I am in the fight” for the title, as eight-time race winner Antonelli is romping towards becoming F1’s youngest ever champion.

A high-pressure situation that Wolff doesn’t think will affect Antonelli, especially thanks to his support network that ensures he remains level-headed for the years to come.

“Kimi from his personality, so grounded, 100% racer, not distracted from anything outside, super family situation and that's why I see no risk that he's losing the plot because he's so dominant,” added Wolff.

Read Also: Formula 1 Russell and Hamilton concede F1 2026 title chances as Antonelli dominates

“Over the next few years, it's something that we will always have our discussions like we have now. What is it that could distract him? What is it that's good for him? What kind of environment he needs? That is the discussion we have.”

“I promise you he's not thinking about it. The way this kid is able to compartmentalise and be the young kid and then get into the car and be the mature racing driver, that's why if Kimi says to himself, I'm not thinking about the championship, he's not thinking about the championship.

“And we are also trying, the parents and myself, the team is saying, you know, this is not finished. There is black swan events. They can come and you're losing something out of your hand when you didn't think it was possible to lose. So he's not going to think about it.”

Sports.title: Haas confident of getting 2027 F1 budget closer to cap with new partner talks
Sports.content:
Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu says the team is making "positive" progress with his team's search for new sponsorship, as the American Formula 1 team seeks to start pushing its yearly budget towards the cap.

F1's smallest team, Haas employs just north of 400 people and has been operating well below the budget cap in both of its iterations. Although the team currently has a title sponsorship deal with Toyota's Gazoo Racing arm, which took over from money transfer company MoneyGram for this year, it is currently looking to further augment its sponsorship portfolio.

Rumours have surfaced that the team is in talks with BWT, currently Alpine's title sponsor, which will move on the team next year as Alpine has a new title partnership with fashion house Gucci planned for 2027. This is not the first time that Haas has been linked to BWT; the Austrian company was suggested as one of its destinations after it ended its deal with Aston Martin at the close of 2021, before it moved to Alpine in search of more pink livery space.

Earlier this year, Komatsu told Sky Sports that a lack of budget was stopping the team from increasing its headcount, and from improving its tooling and infrastructure, and that his job was to find more revenue by attracting new partners to the team.

Speaking over the Madring weekend, Komatsu provided an update and stated that the team was in talks with a few different prospective partners to help bring the team's budget closer to the $215 million cap.

"We're talking to so many prospects; it's getting there. I'd say very positive about next year's budget," Komatsu stated.

"It just helps massively. But I think slowly and surely we are getting our story out there and finding great people. So, yeah, it's good so far."

Asked about the BWT rumours, Komatsu stated that "we're not going to have pink cars, if that's what you are saying!"

Komatsu added that he was not looking to prospective future drivers to make up the shortfall, and that the team was still in a position where it could focus on selecting its 2027 line-up based on performance.

Ayao Komatsu, Haas F1 Team Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

Ryo Hirakawa, Leonardo Fornaroli, and Rafael Camara have been conducting tests in previous cars for Haas, as the team assesses potential future drivers; Komatsu estimated that there were five in the running, presumably including current incumbent Esteban Ocon (whose performances have improved of late) and Yuki Tsunoda.

Asked if any commercial factors would have a bearing, Komatsu stated that it would only enter the picture if he had two drivers who were largely inseparable in terms of pace.

"If it's within a tenth, for instance, very, very close, then affiliation package does come into play for sure. I don't think [that will be the scenario]. I think we can choose by performance; we haven't finished the whole programme yet.

"We really want two fast drivers because that's the best way to grow this team. It doesn't matter if it's two Ferrari drivers or two Toyota drivers or two McLaren drivers.

"I mean, Fornaroli, he's a McLaren driver, right? But honestly, it doesn't matter. Whoever is the fastest, that's the best for the team.

"Again, for everybody, 400 people working here, they need to know that we've got the best driver choice that we can get hold of so that these two drivers are getting the best out of the car. Imagine taking somebody half a second off, but extra money. That's not going to be very motivating.

"And also, one position in the championship. That's quite a lot of money, right? For us, like I said, I'm staying consistent. I've always said we take drivers by performance. That's what we're doing."

Sports.title: F1 reveals 2027 calendar as Monaco joins expanded sprint schedule
Sports.content:
F1 has unveiled its 24-race calendar for the 2027 season, increasing the number of sprint weekends to 10, as it kicks off the season in Bahrain and finishes in Abu Dhabi.

The 2027 season is slated to get underway on 14 March with the Bahrain Grand Prix, which returns to its usual opener slot as a double-header with Saudi Arabia, while Melbourne's Australian Grand Prix becomes the third event on the calendar.

Following events in Japan and China, F1 heads to Miami and Montreal in May. The two events remain three weeks apart, but Canada's 23 May date means the race won't clash with IndyCar's Indy 500.

F1 first heads to Europe with the Monaco Grand Prix on 6 June, which will intriguingly receive a sprint race for the first time despite its tight street circuit not allowing any overtaking. It's understood F1 is keen to lean into Monaco's qualifying spectacle by offering two separate qualifying sessions on Friday and Saturday.

Portugal returns to the calendar for the first time since 2021 with a race at the Algarve circuit in Portimao, taking place on 20 June. The British Grand Prix follows on 4 July at Silverstone, followed by rounds in Austria, Belgium and Hungary, the latter bookending the first half of the season on 1 August.

Bahrain is scheduled to host both pre-season testing and the 2027 season opener Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

After the summer break, action continues in Italy on 5 September, followed by Madrid. Alongside Portugal, Turkey also returns to the calendar on 3 October, as the middle leg of a triple-header with Baku and Singapore.

Another triple-header follows in the Americas with Austin, Mexico and Brazil, while the Las Vegas Grand Prix becomes a standalone race on 20 November.

The season is scheduled to close with a double-header in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, both featuring a sprint format.

Monaco one of 10 rounds to organise a sprint race

Monaco is one of 10 sprint races on the calendar, up from six, as F1 management was keen to expand its number for commercial reasons. Bahrain, Australia, Japan, and Abu Dhabi are also set for a sprint debut, while the format returns to Canada, Britain, Italy, Brazil and Qatar.

"Due to the continued success and strong demand for the format, the number of Sprint events has increased from six to ten for 2027, delivering even more competitive action across the season for fans, promoters, broadcasters, and partners," F1 said in a statement.

"Since the Sprint was introduced in 2021, the data shows that total viewership of Sprint weekends is 12% higher than non-Sprint weekends, Sprint Qualifying is up to three times more popular with fans than Free Practice, 82% of attendees at Sprint weekends say it adds value to their ticket, and 75% of F1 fans believe Sprint events add greater value to a season’s calendar."

Portugal will return to the F1 calendar in 2027 Photo by: Mark Sutton / Motorsport Images

Pre-season testing reverts to a single four-day test in Bahrain from 24-27 February.

As for the conclusion of the 2026 season, F1 is adamant Qatar and Abu Dhabi will go ahead as scheduled until further notice. However, Motorsport.com understands preparations are ongoing in Imola to host the season finale on the Abu Dhabi weekend in the likely scenario that neither Middle Eastern race can take place given the ongoing conflict in the region.

F2 has already added an additional race to its Baku schedule, an indication that the single-seater series is aiming to bolster the end of its season.

“The 2027 calendar brings together some of the most iconic circuits and vibrant cities in the world, creating an incredible stage for another unforgettable season of Formula 1," said F1 CEO and president Stefano Domenicali. "We are thrilled to welcome Portugal and Türkiye to the championship and to expand Sprint racing to ten events, giving our fans even more intensity, drama, and the wheel-to-wheel action that make our sport so special."

“The 2027 FIA Formula One World Championship calendar is a strong reflection of the global appeal and continued growth of our sport," FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem added. "With twenty-four Grands Prix across five continents, the return of Portugal and Türkiye, and the opportunity for an expanded Sprint programme, the calendar combines tradition, innovation, and fan engagement while maintaining the highest sporting standards."

2027 F1 Calendar

12-14 March Bahrain (Sprint) 19-21 March Saudi Arabia 2-4 April Australia (Sprint) 9-11 April Japan (Sprint) 16-18 April China 30 April – 2 May Miami 21-23 May Canada (Sprint) 4-6 June Monaco (Sprint) 18-20 June Portugal 2-4 July Great Britain (Sprint) 9-11 July Austria 23-25 July Belgium 30 July – 1 August Hungary 3-5 September Italy (Sprint) 10-12 September Spain 24-26 September Baku 1-3 October Turkey* 8-10 October Singapore 22-24 October Austin 29-31 October Mexico 5-7 November Brazil (Sprint) 18-20 November Las Vegas 3-5 December Qatar (Sprint) 10-12 December Abu Dhabi (Sprint)

*Subject to FIA circuit homologation

Sports.title: Ferrari not yet switching focus to 2027 F1 car
Sports.content:
Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur says the Scuderia will keep developing its SF-26 Formula 1 car, despite its diminishing title chances.

After Lewis Hamilton retired from the Spanish Grand Prix with brake issues, the seven-time world champion is 101 points adrift of championship leader Kimi Antonelli in the drivers’ standings. Meanwhile, Charles Leclerc finished just fourth at Madring, meaning Ferrari is 145 points down on Mercedes in the constructors’.

Car development resources have to be carefully allocated in light of the cost cap and the aerodynamic testing restrictions; engine-wise, Ferrari has already introduced the two ADUO upgrades it has been allowed.

While teams are known to be working on their 2027 challengers, Vasseur has no intention to make that Ferrari’s full focus just yet.

“We are not in the situation of 12 months ago,” the Frenchman said, referring to F1’s regulatory overhaul for 2026. “Today, what we will develop, we will be able to carry it over on next year's project. We will continue to work, but perhaps on different things, different aspects.

“The development that we do now, 80% will be carried over.”

Frederic Vasseur, Ferrari Photo by: Jayce Illman / Getty Images

As far as Ferrari’s title chances are concerned, Vasseur was asked if it was now ‘game over’ against Antonelli and Mercedes – a question he refused to answer directly.

“Two or three weeks ago I told you that I will take race by race. I didn't change,” he insisted.

The key for Ferrari may be qualifying performance, as Hamilton and Leclerc have both failed to qualify on the front row in any of the four sessions (Zandvoort sprint included) since the summer break. Their average position is fifth, and the SF-26’s deficit to pole has been 0.198s – slower than McLaren and Mercedes, quicker than Red Bull.

“This we need to improve, because I think when you have a look on the pace, during the race the pace is there,” Vasseur said. “For sure we need to do a better job in quali.

“If you take Zandvoort and this one, the profile of the event is a little bit the same for us. We had a decent pace in quali, but we didn't put everything together on the last attempt, and race pace is OK.

“If I have to put the focus of the team on something today, it would be the evolution of the pace during the quali – more than the pace in quali, the evolution, the steps that you can do. We were there on run one Q3, the potential is there, we just have to adapt everything further on.”

Sports.title: Russell and Hamilton concede F1 2026 title chances as Antonelli dominates
Sports.content:
Strange things can happen in Formula 1. Just ask Max Verstappen, who couldn't believe his luck when McLaren handed him a way into the 2025 title fight on a silver platter. Although he eventually missed out by two points to Lando Norris, he was essentially battling with one hand behind his back in an inferior car.

But this year's fight has a distinctly different feel to it. Dominant championship leader Kimi Antonelli has shown fewer, if any, signs of weakness. Mercedes has executed race weekends at a high level - as opposed to rival Ferrari, for example - and it appears to have nixed the most pressing reliability gremlins with the power unit.

Over the European summer, Mercedes was starting to field questions over its lack of development compared to its peers, with a string of four consecutive qualifying defeats starting to make things uncomfortable for Toto Wolff as both Ferrari and McLaren made huge strides with their car.

Did Mercedes, which will only bring significant upgrades to Malaysia in two weeks, get a bit too comfortable courtesy of its early-season dominance?

"I don't think I am in the fight" - Russell

Antonelli's return to winning ways, first with an emotional and staggeringly crushing home victory in Monza and then a slightly more fortunate win in Madrid, has put those questions to bed. After 14 grands prix, Antonelli leads team-mate George Russell by 81 points, with Lewis Hamilton now falling behind triple digits (101) and Norris by 106.

It means Antonelli's biggest threat is now supposed to come from within, but while Russell has stepped up his form in recent weeks with driving style tweaks, it is clear the Briton has no real answer for Antonelli. And even if he were to match his younger team-mate, he is no longer even daring to dream of closing the 81-point deficit.

"I'm not going to say it's over, but it's exceptionally unlikely that I'm in this fight," Russell conceded after only managing fifth at the Madring. "I'm not even thinking about being in the fight because I don't think I am in the fight.

"It almost just allows me to focus race by race and just try and win as many as possible. What will be, will be. That's where we are right now."

Kimi Antonelli and George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Andy Hone/ LAT Images via Getty Images

Earlier this year, it felt Russell was trying to play mind games when he put the onus on 20-year-old Antonelli to bring it home. Now it sounds like he really means it.

If there's no more threat from within for Antonelli, then a late push from Ferrari and McLaren seems like the biggest hurdle.

Speaking to Autosport earlier this month, Ferrari team boss Fred Vasseur vowed his team would push until the end with upgrades, because it also stands the team in good stead for 2027. McLaren made similar comments.

Antonelli and Mercedes have been "phenomenal" - Hamilton

But to the frustration of Hamilton, who had been splitting Antonelli and Russell in the championship this summer, the Scuderia has thrown away too many points with poor race weekend execution, whether in qualifying or the grand prix. A brake failure at the start of the Spanish Grand Prix has now further knocked the wind out of the seven-time world champion's sails.

"Mercedes this year, I think they've done a phenomenal job and they deserve it," Hamilton said as he conceded defeat on Sunday, following similar comments after a frustrating Italian Grand Prix.

"We've just lost so much ground to them [Mercedes] on points. It's tough. I'm giving it everything I can, but sometimes it's just not enough. You need all the other stuff to come together."

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

Meanwhile, all reigning world champion Norris could do was doff his cap at his likely successor given the Italian's age and lack of experience.

"He’s leading by 80 points because he’s doing an incredible job," Norris acknowledged. "He’s beating a much more experienced team-mate, and a decent team-mate. Pretty phenomenal.

"I think it’s cool to see someone so young doing such an incredible job and more than likely go on and win the championship.

"He’s been impressive since the first race this year. Very few mistakes. He’s not driving like it’s his second year in F1, that’s for sure."

Sports.title: Slater to graduate from F3 to F2 for 2027
Sports.content:
Formula 3 runner-up and Audi Formula 1 junior Freddie Slater will step up to Formula 2 with Invicta Racing in 2027.

The 2024 Italian F4 and 2025 Formula Regional European champion was signed by Audi to spearhead its new Driver Development Programme in 2026, while he moved to F3 with Trident.

Four consecutive feature-race podiums meant Slater snatched the lead of the championship away from sophomore Ugo Ugochukwu going into the summer break, but he only scored 15 more points across the last five races of the season and was surpassed by the Campos driver in the title battle.

Read Also: Formula 1 Ugochukwu beats Slater to win F3 title

Slater still was the best rookie of the season – though he did take part in two rounds in 2025. Eight podiums including one victory in Hungary meant the 18-year-old Briton comfortably took the runner-up spot ahead of second-year Tuukka Taponen and fellow debutant Taito Kato.

“I’m really excited to be stepping up to Formula 2 with Invicta Racing next year,” Slater said. “I learned a lot in Formula 3 this season, and I feel I have developed as a driver and as a person over the course of the year.

“Invicta has a great record in Formula 2, and I cannot wait to get started with the team and prepare for our campaign together. I am also very grateful for the continued support from the Audi Driver Development Programme. There is still a lot for me to learn, and I’m really looking forward to taking on this new challenge.”

Rafael Camara, Invicta Racing Photo by: Clive Mason / Getty Images

The Trident-to-Invicta pipeline has been extremely successful in recent years with several instances of back-to-back titles.

Gabriel Bortoleto, Leonardo Fornaroli and Rafael Camara earned the previous three F3 crowns with the Italian squad, before switching to the Norfolk-based outfit in F2 – where Bortoleto and Fornaroli became champions as rookies. Currently a close second in the 2026 standings, Camara has a decent chance of emulating them.

Even though he narrowly failed to prevail in F3, these are the examples Slater will aim to follow in 2027.

“The move to Formula 2 is the natural next step for Freddie, and an important new phase of his development as a driver,” said Audi Driver Development Programme director Allan McNish.

“He enjoyed a strong Formula 3 season, fighting for the title until the final round – showing his speed, racecraft and progress throughout the year. We are very proud of what Freddie has achieved this season and how he has developed along the way.

“Invicta Racing has had an excellent record in recent years, and we are delighted to be working with them. We believe it is the ideal environment for him, and we look forward to supporting him as he takes on this new challenge in 2027.”

Sports.title: Norris completes first full test in McLaren’s Le Mans Hypercar
Sports.content:
Reigning Formula 1 champion Lando Norris completed his first full-fledged test at the wheel of the McLaren MCL-HY Le Mans Hypercar at Portimao on Monday.

Following last weekend’s Spanish Grand Prix at the new Madring circuit in which he was denied victory by an ill-timed Virtual Safety Car, Norris travelled across the border to Portugal for a one-day test.

The Briton completed 38 laps of the Algarve International Circuit in the V6-powered challenger, logging a total of 177 miles through the day. McLaren said his programme included testing several development items and providing feedback through his immense experience in F1.

Norris was assisted in his first LMDh test by McLaren’s 2027 drivers Mikkel Jensen and Laurens Vanthoor, who carried out further development work ahead of the British brand’s Hypercar debut next year.

"First of all, a big thanks to the McLaren Hypercar Team for letting me drive the MCL-HY,” he said.

“It was great for them to give me a chance to have a bit of fun and try something new, particularly during their busy preparations for next year.

“I think we also collected some valuable data, and I hope I was able to bring a different set of feelings, comments, and perspectives on things, which is useful for the team in this crucial testing period.

“It was cool for me personally to work with this team, and it was exciting to try new machinery too. I've not done a proper test in anything other than an F1 car for years now, so the fact I got to try something different, especially still as part of the McLaren family, was very special.

“It was a fun day in a quick car on a cool track, helping the team prepare for the start of WEC next year. A big thanks to everyone involved, I can't wait to get back in the car in the future.”

Monday’s test follows Norris sampling the MCL-HY for the first time at the car’s public debut at the Goodwood Festival of the Speed in July.

McLaren Racing boss Zak Brown had previously shown interest in fielding both Norris and Oscar Piastri in the World Endurance Championship’s blue-riband event, although any such outing may rely on the team running an additional third car.

A Le Mans outing would only be possible if there are no clashes with Norris’ F1 commitments next year.

While the full 2027 WEC calendar was already revealed three months ago, with Le Mans pencilled in for the weekend of 12-13 June, F1 is yet to publish its schedule for next year amid the war in West Asia.

Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: McLaren

Speaking on Monday, McLaren Hypercar team principal James Barclay left the door open for further outings for Norris in the future, without explicitly referring to any race appearances.

“We are all racers at McLaren Racing, and competing in Formula 1, INDYCAR and the World Endurance Championship creates exciting cross-series opportunities,” he said.

“Lando was keen to drive the MCL-HY beyond his Goodwood Hill run, so we invited him to join our private Portimão test. As we fully expected he adapted very quickly, integrated seamlessly and provided valuable feedback to support the car’s development.

"It was a pleasure to have him with the team, we wish him every success for the rest of the Formula 1 season, and we look forward to welcoming him back into the McLaren Hypercar Team soon.”

Sports.title: F2 adds extra Baku feature race and insists Qatar, Abu Dhabi still on – what does this mean for F1?
Sports.content:
The Formula 2 championship has announced a "supersized" meeting for its next round in Baku. The move will see it host an additional feature race in Azerbaijan and comes just 10 days before the race weekend is due to kick off.

It is an unusual and late decision that inevitably raises eyebrows at a time when the end of the Formula 1 season remains uncertain. At present, the Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix could potentially be unable to go ahead as planned due to the tense geopolitical situation in the Middle East.

In practical terms, what the F2 organisers announced on Monday, just over a week before the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, is a double-header weekend, with an additional qualifying session and feature race compared to the usual format.

"As Formula 2 is the only support event at the Azerbaijan Formula 1 Grand Prix, together with the promoters, we have opted for a supersized F2 race weekend, with one free practice, two qualifying sessions, one sprint race and two feature races," F2 CEO Bruno Michel confirmed.

"This is the only weekend where the timetable allows the additional sessions, which will increase the level of entertainment even further for the attending crowd and all our fans. The Baku City Circuit always provides us with amazing racing, so we’re very pleased to make the 12th Round of our season pretty unique."

The organisers have not specified exactly why they chose to expand the Baku meeting, but it is difficult not to see it - without being able to say so for certain - as a way of preparing for the cancellation or reshaping of some of the end-of-season events and compensating for the points that would be lost as a result.

The F2 season finale is still scheduled for Abu Dhabi Photo by: Dom Gibbons / LAT Images via Getty Images

"The final two rounds of the season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will resume with the usual weekend format made of one free practice followed by one qualifying, a sprint race and a feature race," F2 said in a statement.

That is the situation today, but it could quickly change depending on the decisions made by F1 regarding the end of the season.

The FIA and F1 are expected to decide on the remainder of the 2026 calendar before the end of the month, with a relocated Bahrain Grand Prix at Sepang, Malaysia, already added for early October.

Among the options recently discussed is the possibility of cancelling the trips to Qatar and Abu Dhabi and heading to Imola in late November for the season final instead.

Sports.title: Monaco to hold first sprint race as F1 increases total to 10 on 2027 calendar | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 has announced its calendar for the 2027 season and increased the total number of sprint events to 10.

The 2027 F1 calendar will therefore include a record total of 34 races.

Despite concerns over the viability of racing in the Middle East, the championship has announced its 2027 season will begin and end with back-to-back rounds in the region.

The championship will open and close with sprint events in Bahrain and Abu Dhabi. This year’s Bahrain Grand Prix has been relocated to Malaysia due to the ongoing war in Iran, but Formula One Management says next year’s season-opener will take place at the Bahrain International Circuit.

Saudi Arabia’s Jeddah Corniche Circuit, which was dropped from this year’s calendar due to the war, is slated to hold the second round of the season.

The status of this year’s season-ending races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi remains in doubt. Formula 1 CEO Stefano has previously indicated a decision on whether those events will go ahead will be announced in mid-September, but F1’s statement on its 2027 calendar made no reference to the situation.

The cancellation of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix reduced the total number of events on this year’s calendar from 24 to 23. Providing all next year’s events take place, the calendar will return to a total of 24 rounds. As previously announced, Zandvoort in the Netherlands and the Circuit de Catalunya in Spain will lose their events, while new rounds in Portugal and Turkey join the calendar.

The total number of sprint events will increase from six to 10 next year. Although F1 originally announced the format would be used at “tracks with great overtaking potential”, next year’s calendar includes a sprint event at Monte-Carlo in Monaco, widely regarded as the hardest track to overtake on.

Four other venues will also hold sprint events for the first time: Bahrain, Melbourne in Australia, Suzuka in Japan and Yas Marina in Abu Dhabi. For the first time the opening race of the season will be a sprint race and the final round will also be a sprint event.

None of the 24 events clash with the Indianapolis 500, Le Mans 24 Hours or Nurburgring 24 Hours.

Sports.title: Stats: Mercedes equal Ferrari as Formula 1’s most successful engine builders by race wins | 2026 Spanish Grand Prix stats and facts
Sports.content:
Mercedes’ new star driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli delivered a milestone moment for the manufacturer with his victory in the Spanish Grand Prix.

Antonelli’s latest triumph was the 251st victory for a Mercedes-powered car in the history of the world championship. It puts them level with the most famous and historic name in the series, Ferrari.

Mercedes have achieved this despite contesting far fewer grands prix than their rivals. Both were active in the fifties, but Mercedes disappeared for four decades after the horrific deaths of the 1955 Le Mans 24 Hours.

Since their return with McLaren in the nineties, Mercedes have consistently been a force to be reckoned with. Ferrari dominated the early noughts but after Mercedes returned with their own factory team they enjoyed an unprecedented run of success the following decade.

Although the factory team had a difficult few seasons prior to this year, McLaren’s return to form helped to sustain the winning rate of their engine division. With Mercedes back on form this year, it has long seemed inevitable they would catch and eventually equal Ferrari’s tally:

*Season in progress

However Mercedes’ works team still lags far behind Ferrari’s in terms of total wins. McLaren scored more than 100 of the victories powered by Mercedes engines, while Brawn GP (2009) and Racing Point (2020) also contributed to Mercedes’ tally.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

In contrast, only a single race has ever been won by a Ferrari customer team: Sebastian Vettel’s 2008 Italian Grand Prix victory for Toro Rosso:

Mercedes’ record-equalling win came courtesy of Antonelli’s eighth career victory. That gives him as many as 1967 world champion Denny Hulme, plus Jacky Ickx and Daniel Ricciardo. It’s also one more than his team mate George Russell has scored.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Russell netted the 12th fastest lap of his career. That puts him level with rival Sergio Perez, as well as multiple world champions Alberto Ascari and Jack Brabham, plus Rene Arnoux and Juan Pablo Montoya.

Max Verstappen remains yet to score a win this season, but did claim second place in his 250th appearance in a grand prix weekend. He should make his 250th start in Singapore.

Lewis Hamilton failed to score for the first time this year. He was the last remaining driver to have taken points at every weekend and hadn’t finished outside the top six until his brake failure on Sunday.

For the first time since 2012, Spain held two rounds of the world championship. That year saw the final appearance of Valencia’s street track, an unloved venue which the Madring drew immediate comparisons with.

The Madring is the seventh different Spanish circuit to host F1. It joins Pedralbes, Jarama, Montjuich Park, Jerez, the Circuit de Catalunya and Valencia. France has also hosted F1 at seven different tracks but the only country with more grand prix venues is the USA, with 12.

There was little for the home crowd to celebrate in Madrid, however: Fernando Alonso and Carlos Sainz Jnr collided with each other and neither spent a single lap inside the top 10.

Sports.title: ‘Realistically I’m not in the fight for the drivers’ championship’ admits Russell | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s closest championship rival admits he does not have a realistic chance of beating him to the title this year.

George Russell lies 81 points behind his team mate with 233 available over the remaining rounds. He hasn’t gained on Antonelli since the British Grand Prix two months ago.

Russell finished fifth in Sunday’s race at the Madring, almost half a minute behind his race-winning team mate, after making a second pit stop. But after struggling with his car earlier in the season, Russell says recent rounds have gone better.

“It has been a more positive couple of races even though the result was far from great today,” said Russell on Sunday. “But it’s kind of the story of the season.

“I just need to focus on the performance and keep trying to help the team. We’re obviously in a great place to win the constructors’ [championship]. Realistically I’m not in the fight for the drivers and that just allows me just to focus on race-by-race and trying to focus on just getting some good results.”

Russell led the championship after the first two rounds but Antonelli moved ahead at the Japanese Grand Prix. He scored his eighth win on Sunday while Russell only has two victories so far this season.

Antonelli said he will not relent as he bids to clinch the world championship. “It’s great, but we’ve just got to keep pushing, keep delivering the results and just trying to do the best job I can whenever I go on track,” he said.

“Because of course, yes, I have a big lead, but you never know what can happen. So I just need to be ready for anything and keep maximising every opportunity I get, and then we’ll see where we end up at the end of the year.”

Sports.title: Pictures: Norris tests McLaren’s MCL-HY WEC hypercar at Algarve | Other Motorsport
Sports.content:
Lando Norris had his first run in McLaren’s new World Endurance Championship hypercar following the Spanish Grand Prix.

The reigning Formula 1 world champion drove the car at the Autodromo do Algarve in Portugal.

McLaren will enter the WEC’s top tier next season. “It was great for them to give me a chance to have a bit of fun and try something new, particularly during their busy preparations for next year,” said Norris.

“I think we also collected some valuable data, and I hope I was able to bring a different set of feelings, comments, and perspectives on things, which is useful for the team in this crucial testing period.”

F1 will return to the Algarve circuit next year, for the first time since 2021. Norris previously drove the car in a brief demonstration run at the Goodwood Festival of Speed.

“It was cool for me personally to work with this team, and it was exciting to try new machinery too,” Norris continued. “I’ve not done a proper test in anything other than an F1 car for years now, so the fact I got to try something different, especially still as part of the McLaren family, was very special.”

McLaren hypercar team principal James Barclay said “Lando was keen to drive the MCL-HY beyond his Goodwood Hill run, so we invited him to join our private Portimao test.”

“As we fully expected he adapted very quickly, integrated seamlessly and provided valuable feedback to support the car’s development,” he added.

Almost no one had anything positive to say about Formula 1’s newest circuit following the first Spanish Grand Prix yesterday.

One point which several readers made about the Madring, echoed by Lando Norris in the press conference after the race, was why the designers of the hybrid track had created a layout so narrow, twisty and difficult for cars to race closely on:

It was absolutely terrible. I saw someone say they enjoyed FP4, which more or less covers it. But I want to give it a zero [out of 10], because the track was so avoidably terrible. It’s not a once-good track that has been outgrown, like Monaco, or a circuit designed using supposedly sound theory that just didn’t work, like Abu Dhabi. They had a more or less blank slate and (I can only assume deliberately, as no one is dense enough to have done that by accident) created a track it’s impossible to actually race on. I’ve been watching F1 for over 30 years and (having spent some time reflecting to avoid recency bias) the Madring is the worst circuit, for its generation of cars, that I have ever seen.

Sports.title: Norris sure McLaren were right to pit him immediately after the VSC | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lando Norris defended McLaren’s tactics after he lost his chance to win yesterday’s Spanish Grand Prix during a Virtual Safety Car period.

The McLaren driver was leading from Andrea Kimi Antonelli and Max Verstappen when a VSC period began on lap 15. Norris passed the pit lane entrance before the VSC was triggered, but Antonelli and all the other drivers had the chance to pit before it ended.

The VSC period ended before Norris returned to the pit lane entrance. McLaren summoned him in anyway, despite not having the opportunity to pit while the cars were lapping slowly. Norris’s misfortune was compounded by a problem with his right-front wheel which slowed his pit stop.

Other drivers such as Charles Leclerc opted not to pit at this time, extending their first stint. However they started the race on the hard compound, while Norris was on mediums. He believes pitting immediately after the VSC was the best choice for him.

“I had to come in at the end of the lap because it was the only chance,” Norris explained. “It was still effectively some pit loss, the fact that everyone’s on colder tyres [means] you’re still minimising the pit loss. The medium tyre was destroyed and the hard tyre was amazing.”

Norris said he was “just unfortunate” with the timing of the VSC period but he was able to close on Antonelli and Verstappen after they closed on Leclerc.

“The pace was very, very strong on the hard tyre. I know they were stuck [but] we caught up 13, 14 seconds or more, almost.

“So there’s plenty of positives. A day full of positives, just one thing let it all down.”

Asked whether McLaren should have anticipated a VSC period would be triggered after Lance Stroll stopped in a run-off area, Norris said: “I need to speak to the pit wall. I’m just driving the car, I don’t know these things.

“So, I need to go speak to the team and see what else. But it’s not the team’s fault, it’s not my fault. Simple as that. We were just unlucky.”

Sports.title: Queensberry Wins Janibek Bid, Sheeraz Gets $751,357
Sports.content:
The modest purse leaves Sheeraz cornered, forcing him to choose between risking his belt or openly swerving the most dangerous assignment out there. Sheeraz spent weeks laying the groundwork for an exit, complaining on the Mr. Verzace Podcast that the money would come in considerably low for what he admitted was the stiffest challenge of his career. That talk was an obvious insurance policy designed to soften the blow if he decides to run for the hills.

Now that the numbers are locked in, walking away will look terrible for the champion. Dropping the strap to avoid Janibek will be viewed as a blatant duck, cementing the perception that Sheeraz wants no part of a genuine elite puncher. Fleeing the division to jump into Zuffa Boxing might protect his record inside an in-house roster, but it leaves his reputation in shreds.

Queensberry has zero reason to play along with that escape plan. Feeding Sheeraz another soft touch on his way out the door does nothing for Frank Warren. A meaningless showcase fails to move the needle on DAZN, leaves arena seats empty, and merely protects Sheeraz’s market value for a rival promoter.

Warren ought to hold Sheeraz’s feet to the fire by demanding the hardest fight on the board. Janibek remains the obvious choice since the purse bid is settled. If Sheeraz bolts, Queensberry should pivot straight to Osleys Iglesias, Diego Pacheco, or rugged contenders Kevin Lele Sadjo and Jacob Bank.

If Sheeraz somehow faces Janibek or Iglesias and wins, Queensberry sends him off with a legitimate, signature victory. If he loses, the bubble bursts before Zuffa cuts him a massive check.

That hype train already suffered major damage in July. Simon Zachenhuber dragged Sheeraz into deep water, trapping him against the ropes, battering his guard, and making him look utterly ordinary. Escaping with a questionable majority decision wiped away the shine from the Edgar Berlanga knockout and exposed glaring flaws in Sheeraz’s game.

Fans watched Sheeraz struggle with an unheralded opponent, and the consensus right now is that Janibek would dismantle him. Vacating the title to chase Iglesias or Pacheco might salvage a shred of credibility by showing money was the issue. Vacating just to hide against another Alem Begic or Zachenhuber-tier fighter makes the verdict academic. It would confirm Sheeraz ran scared from a test he knew he could not pass.

Sports.title: Chris Mannix Blasts Nico Ali Walsh’s Boxing Bill Support
Sports.content:
Senator Ted Cruz spotlighted Walsh’s endorsement ahead of the vote, crediting him with securing vital amendments. Walsh testified against the draft in April, but reversed his stance after lawmakers added shorter terms, free agency rules, ranking oversight, and mandatory financial reporting.

Under the new terms, an initial Unified Boxing Organization deal cannot exceed three years, subsequent deals cap at six years, and boxers get a 90-day negotiating window before agreements expire.

Mannix remains focused on the concentration of control. A UBO could sign fighters, stage fights, manage rankings, and hand out championship belts. Merging those regulatory and promotional roles under one roof directly upends decades of customary divisions in the sport.

Walsh raised that exact warning during his April testimony. He highlighted how UFC competitors capture less than 20 percent of event revenue, whereas top boxers command the vast majority. Major league team sports use centralized systems, but their players rely on labor unions to negotiate wages and revenue splits. The Senate bill offers boxers no similar collective voice.

Promotional bidding wars drive boxer pay. A premier UBO armed with exclusive broadcast distribution, proprietary belts, and internal rankings would neutralize outside competition. Boxers might hit free agency after three years, but departing the ecosystem would mean giving up their titles and standing.

A $200 per round wage floor offers modest help to preliminary fighters. It provides zero protection for contenders whose earning power depends on competing offers. Walsh secured contractual adjustments, but Mannix points out that Cruz can now leverage the Ali legacy to establish unprecedented corporate control over the sport.

Sports.title: Sanchez Calls Benn A Carcass, Favors Teofimo Over Ryan
Sports.content:
“I would have to give Teo the advantage a little bit because Ryan was in against a guy that was depleted, a guy that was a carcass of himself,” Sanchez told Fight Hub TV. “How do you gauge Ryan for the future? It wasn’t somebody that was there 100%. Tio fought somebody that was there 100% and gave him a fight. For those reasons, I have to give the edge to Teo.”

Benn reportedly jumped from 146 pounds at Friday’s weigh-in to an astonishing 178.4 pounds by that night. Ryan did his job by liquidating a vulnerable target immediately, but finishing an empty shell in four minutes leaves major questions about his engine at the new weight.

Those answers mean something against someone with Teofimo’s championship pedigree. Ryan has yet to prove his speed and snap hold up over twelve rounds at 147. Lopez already knows how to ride out rough water, having worked through testing moments against Sandor Martin, Josh Taylor, and Rolly Romero without losing his head. Sanchez expects Lopez to control center ring through measured pressure rather than wild swarming. Lopez relies on feints and lateral steps to dictate distance, a tactic that forces Ryan to build offense from scratch instead of waiting for a target to run directly into a counter.

Walking Ryan down carries clear danger. Lopez must shave away distance without stepping into the left hook. Teofimo also has a habit of getting cocky once he feels in control, giving opponents free openings to get back in the contest. Teofimo still brings the deeper bag of tools. He counters in flurries, digs to the body, and switches cadence when his primary game plan meets resistance. Ryan, on the other hand, remains heavily dependent on timing that single explosive bomb.

Sanchez views the clash as practically dead-even while giving Lopez the slight nod. Ryan brings superior reach, height, and raw hand speed. Teofimo counters with ring craft, distance control, and the ring sense to adjust under fire.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua Chooses Britain After Testing American Price
Sports.content:
Hearn now says Joshua had two offers in front of him after the American financial package was worked out.

“We set out some terms where it might be able to agree. The money that we discussed ultimately probably was deliverable, was agreed. Anthony turned around to me with the two offers on the table and said, ‘No, I just want to stick to the original contract. I want to do this fight in the UK.’ Anthony Joshua could have taken many millions more to do the fight in America. That is why the fight will not be taking place in America, because Anthony Joshua is not a sellout,” said Hearn to iFL TV.

That final line is wonderfully theatrical. Joshua rejected more money, but only after Hearn had submitted terms for moving the fight to America and received indications that the requested package was deliverable.

Joshua was not indifferent to money. He considered the enhanced American offer and then decided it was less valuable than fighting at home. Remaining in Britain also protects Joshua’s commercial relationship with the audience that built him. Taking the largest all-British heavyweight fight to New York for a larger purse risked angering supporters who will help sustain his value after boxing.

Keeping the event under its original UK agreement also leaves Dana White and Zuffa Boxing outside the promotion, an outcome Hearn plainly will not regret. White and Nick Khan pushed for Madison Square Garden and tried persuading Joshua to accept the switch.

British fans have not won everything. Hearn is willing to accept a main event beginning around 1 a.m. to give Netflix a stronger American viewing window. The crowd gets Cardiff, but overseas viewers still receive the convenient hour.

Hearn also dismissed November 28, telling iFL TV interviewer Kugan Cassius, “I think you need new sources.” He advised supporters not to book anything before the official announcement.

Cardiff remains an option rather than a completed deal. Hearn said confirmation of a UK fight may arrive within the next week.

Sports.title: Sugar Ray Leonard Wrenches Glory From Thomas Hearns
Sports.content:
Hearns was just 22 years old, carrying a pristine 32-0 record with 30 knockouts into the ring. Standing 6 foot 1, he owned significant height and reach edges over the 5 foot 10 Leonard. Those physical realities dictated the early flow of the contest.

Hearns established his long left jab immediately, denying Leonard the separation required to unload rapid combinations. Leonard’s left eye began to shut, while Hearns banked rounds behind sharp outside boxing.

The matchup forced Leonard to ditch his trademark style. His speed and ring circles failed to pierce Hearns’ reach. To survive, Leonard had to absorb clean leather, barrel inside, and morph into a pure pressure brawler.

The adjustment broke through in round six when Leonard stunned Hearns with a vicious left hook. Leonard poured on punishment through round seven, hammering Hearns with heavy flurries that had the Detroit fighter wobbling on rubbery legs. Neither frame produced an official knockdown, and all three judges scored them 10-9.

Hearns regrouped with poise. Refusing to trade, he relied on his jab and lateral steps to dictate rounds nine through twelve. Leonard stalked without landing sufficient blows, his injured eye worsening by the minute.

After round twelve, trainer Angelo Dundee delivered the famous corner rallying cry: “You’re blowing it now, son! You’re blowing it!”

Dundee saw the reality clearly. Leonard had completely run out of room for error.

Leonard surged forward in round thirteen, cracking Hearns with a sharp right hand. Hearns tumbled through the ring ropes, yet referee Davey Pearl ruled the sequence a slip. That decision offered Hearns precious recovery time while robbing Leonard of an automatic 10-8 cushion. Leonard kept pressing anyway, flooring Hearns before the bell sounded.

The onslaught resumed in the fourteenth. Leonard rocked Hearns with an overhand right, backed him into the ropes, and fired unanswered punches until Pearl intervened at the 1:45 mark.

Hearns stayed on his feet, prompting protests from his camp. In truth, his guard was gone, his legs were shot, and Leonard was punishing a defenseless opponent.

Judges Duane Ford, Lou Tabat, and Chuck Minker held Hearns ahead by two to four points entering the fourteenth round. Leonard did not merely edge out an opponent down the stretch. He wrenched the crown away from a fighter who had outworked him over the long haul.

Eight years later, Hearns scored two clean knockdowns against Leonard only to walk away with a controversial draw. The two bouts defined their historic rivalry: Hearns possessed the tools to outbox Leonard over long distances, but Leonard carried the ferocious resolve required to overcome disaster when the bell rang.

Sports.title: O’Shaquie Foster Risks Fighting Emanuel Navarrete’s Fight
Sports.content:
O’Shaquie Foster wants Emanuel Navarrete to know he won’t retreat in their October 24 junior lightweight unification bout. That promise sounds great for the cameras, yet planting his feet gives Navarrete the exact environment he thrives on.

“I’m gonna control the fight,” Foster told The Ring. “I’m gonna dominate from Round One. I ain’t never ran from nobody. I put punishment and pain to my opponents as well. That night, he’s gonna get a boxing lesson.”

Navarrete looked sharp in February when he stopped Eduardo “Sugar” Nunez inside ten rounds. It was a far crisper display than his May 2025 outing with Charly Suarez, which was halted in the eighth round because of a cut before being changed to a no contest. Nunez marched directly into Navarrete and got dismantled by awkward uppercuts, bruising body work, and relentless output. Navarrete never had to expend energy tracking him down. Nunez stayed within reach, allowing the Mexican champion to unload long flurries without interruption.



Foster risks walking into that identical trap if machismo dictates his strategy. His crisp straight shots will land, as Navarrete consistently drops his hands when winding up. Still, clean punches to the jaw have never discouraged Navarrete. Foster simply does not possess the concussive power required to make him freeze. Trading in close quarters invites physical exhaustion alongside scoring problems. Navarrete can bank rounds purely on volume while leaning on Foster with heavy forearm shivers, collar ties, and rib-cracking hooks. That constant grinding will take the spring out of Foster’s legs when he needs them most. Foster secures his best path by scoring with sharp counters, stepping off at angles, and making Navarrete constantly reset his feet. He can deliver the tactical schooling he envisions, yet trying to prove his bravado will turn the contest into a grueling brawl built for Navarrete. Facebook

Sports.title: Jesus Ramos Jr. Talking Adames And Yoenli While Ignoring The Danger In Front Of Him
Sports.content:
Nursultanov has spent three full years on the shelf. That kind of inactivity invites dismissal, yet it creates a blind spot for the camp. Ramos is preparing for an opponent frozen in time.

“I just got to get him out of the way, get Meiirim out of the way, and focus on [Adames],” Ramos Jr.said to Sean Zittell. “In a perfect world, I fight Adames, Yoenli fights for the WBA, and we fight. Both on the line, WBC, WBA, unify. That’s a great fight, too.”

That roadmap falls apart if Nursultanov plays spoiler. The Kazakh brings a clean 20-0 record with 11 knockouts alongside heavy amateur seasoning. His classic style relies on an upright European posture, an active jab, and a shell defense. Those traits mirror the tactical issues that derailed Ramos against Erickson Lubin. Lubin stayed disciplined, refused to trade in the pocket, and tagged Ramos as he marched forward. Nursultanov fights out of an orthodox stance, but he possesses the tools to punish reckless pressure if Ramos stalks without establishing his range.

The extended layoff complicates preparation. Ramos acknowledged his corner watched minimal film because fresh footage does not exist. Nursultanov used the downtime to quietly recalibrate his habits away from scouting cameras.

Physical readiness brings its own questions. Ramos returns from persistent hand issues that shelved him following his victory over Shane Mosley Jr. No bones broke, and surgeons stayed away, but swelling kept him out of action. Slamming punches against Nursultanov’s elbows and tight gloves will provide an immediate answer about whether those hands are truly healed.

The WBC track already lays out the next step. The winner gets full champion Carlos Adames. Talk of chasing Yoenli Hernandez is pure promotional fantasy right now.

Ramos cannot afford to look past the ring apron. His focus belongs entirely on solving Nursultanov, or he will relive the bitter lessons of the Lubin defeat.

Sports.title: Teddy Atlas Sees Different Devin Haney Rematch
Sports.content:
“He’s a sharpshooter when he boxes right. He didn’t box right against Garcia. He tried to go get Garcia. That’s not him. He’s a guy that sets traps. He’s real accurate with his punches. He doesn’t waste anything. He’s a consummate boxer, counterpuncher, and he didn’t fight. He came out of character against Garcia, and he paid a price for it,” Atlas said on The Fight with Teddy Atlas.

While Atlas suggests Haney is back to his old self, beating Norman is a completely different assignment than dealing with Garcia. Norman did not possess the specific weapon that gave Haney nightmares, nor did he wage psychological warfare for two months leading up to the opening bell. A second promotion would immediately bring up the failed drug tests, the civil lawsuit, and the three knockdowns Haney suffered in Brooklyn. Remaining calm against a standard contender in a sterile build is easy compared to keeping cool while Garcia mocks you on a public stage.

Beyond the mental aspect, the physical danger has not changed. Haney still tends to reach with his jab, leaning over his front knee and leaving his chin exposed along the exact angle Garcia targets with his left hook. Tightening his right hand can mitigate some risk, but recovering his guard fast enough to beat Garcia’s hand speed is another matter entirely.

Moving to welterweight does offer Haney better durability after years of draining down to 140 pounds, yet extra mass often costs a boxer a step of foot speed. If Haney becomes too tentative out of respect for Garcia’s power, he risks giving away rounds by waiting too long to pull the trigger.

Atlas sees a transformed fighter, but Ryan already knows he can crack Haney’s chin. Until Haney proves he can take that left hook flush and keep his composure under heavy fire, one solid bounce-back win does not erase the blueprint Garcia put on film.

Calling Haney improved because he survived against Jose Ramirez and Brian Norman Jr. ignores what actually took place inside those ropes. He looked gun-shy, skittish, and terrified of taking a flush shot. Against Ramirez, Haney did not put on a masterclass. He fought an aging, faded pressure fighter who was tailor-made for a clean counter-punching showcase. Instead of setting traps and letting his hands go with authority, Haney was on his bicycle, grabbing in close, and throwing single shots just to scrape rounds on the scorecards.

When a fighter lands barely five or six punches a round and spends the rest of the time tying up, that is not growth. That is damage control. The Norman fight was even more revealing. Norman had crude technique, zero experience at the elite level, and spent half the night lunging into empty air.

A prime, confident Haney would have picked him apart with sharp combinations and controlled the pocket. Instead, Haney looked shell-shocked the moment Norman tried to apply physical pressure. Haney held constantly, smothered his own work, and moved defensively without setting up any real offense to discourage Norman.

Surviving twelve rounds by spoiling and clutching is a survival reflex, not technical improvement. Haney’s chin and confidence took a permanent dent when Garcia repeatedly bounced that left hook off his head in Brooklyn. Now, whenever an opponent steps forward with bad intentions, Haney defaults to frantic clinching and lateral retreat. He might have the decision wins on his record, but the tape tells a completely different story.

Haney is fighting scared, fighting negative, and hiding behind excessive holding because he knows he can no longer trust his chin. Against punchers who do not care about his feather-fisted counters, that nervous, safety-first approach is a ticking time bomb.

Ghana News.title: MTN@30: Three customers drive away brand-new Land Cruiser Prado in Kumasi
Ghana News.content:
MTN Ghana has rewarded three of its loyal customers with brand-new Toyota Land Cruiser Prado as part of its 30th anniversary celebrations, at a ceremony held at the Kejetia Market in Kumasi.

The winners, Faustina Asante, a beverage trader; Wasila Mahama, a farmer; and Halidu Tanko, an engineer emerged from the MTN@30 Mega Promo, a usage-based campaign launched in June 2026 and ending in August.

MTN Ghana, which has operated in the country for three decades, has built a large customer base through its telecommunications and digital financial services, including mobile money, data and voice services.

Senior Consumer Marketing Manager of MTN Ghana, Sandra Owusu Antwi, said the anniversary promotion was introduced to appreciate customers for their continued support while rewarding their everyday use of MTN services.

“This year, MTN we are celebrating 30 years anniversary, 30 years of being in Ghana, connecting our customers. As part of it, we introduced the MTN at 30 mega promo, the mega promo was introduced three months ago and it’s a usage based promo. Meaning when you do what you normally do, all goes into your usage and with as little as 30 pesewas gets you into the promo. The promo is throughout the whole country,” she noted.

She said MTN is giving out nine cars in total, alongside other prizes, to customers participating in the promotion.

“We will be giving out as many as 30,000 customers to receive various cash rewards on this promo. The promo has come to an end and this is the second presentation that we’ve done. The third one will happen few weeks to come. First one happened in Accra-Madina market, second one which is Kumasi-Kejetia,” she noted.

Mrs Antwi added that customers should expect more opportunities and rewards from MTN as the company continues to celebrate its 30 years of operations in Ghana.

For winner Faustina Asante, her frequent use of MTN Mobile Money and voice services in her beverage business contributed to her participation in the promotion.

“I thank God and secondly thank MTN. I was scrolling through TikTok and chanced on MTN video where they said they’re giving out cars to customers. I called my son to check for me which he even said it isn’t true unless I stake and I told I want to because the car is very nice and for that matter, I did and I was able to become one of the winners,” she asserted.

Another winner, Wasila Mahama, said she increased her purchases of airtime and data after seeing an  about the promotion.

“It was an advert I watched and decided to buy more data bundle and airtime. I was even doing data bundle do my friends. I didn’t believe I’d become a winner but I thank God I have been able to be a part of the winners. I encourage everyone to participate in any MTN promo that will be introduced,” she said.

For Halidu Tanko, an engineer and an MTN customer since 1996, his regular transactions, including Mobile Money and airtime purchases, earned him an opportunity to win.

“It is the normal transaction I was doing. MoMo, buying airtime for the last 3 months. I’ve used MTN for a very long time since 1996 and I’ve come out successful. I thank MTN,” he said.

The Kumasi presentation is the second major vehicle presentation under the MTN@30 Mega Promo, with the remaining three Land Cruiser Prado expected to be presented in the next phase of the promotion.

Senior Specialist, Mass Segment at MTN Ghana, Maxwell Arthur, said the promotion was designed to give customers a share in the company’s 30th anniversary celebrations.

“Ghanaians have supported us very well and because of that we decided that Ghanaians also benefit from this anniversary celebration for the support they’ve given us. We are giving out nine Land Cruiser Prados which we’ve given out three already and we’re giving out three today too and we’ll give out the other three in the next month.
